verses.1:1: I made the first account, Theophilus, concerning all that Jesus began both to do and to teach,
verses.1:2: until the day on which, having given commands through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom He had chosen, He was taken up.
verses.1:3: To them He also presented Himself alive after His suffering by many sure proofs, appearing to them during forty days and speaking the things concerning the kingdom of God.
verses.1:4: And while eating with them, He commanded them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father, "which you heard from Me,
verses.1:5: for John baptized with water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit not many days from now."
verses.1:6: So when they had come together, they were asking Him, saying, "Lord, is it at this time that You are restoring the kingdom to Israel?"
verses.1:7: He said to them, "It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has set in His own authority,
verses.1:8: but you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be My witnesses both in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the farthest part of the earth."
verses.1:9: And having said these things, while they were watching, He was lifted up, and a cloud took Him up from their eyes.
verses.1:10: And as they were gazing intently into heaven while He was going, look, two men stood beside them in white garments,
verses.1:11: who also said, "Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in this same manner in which you watched Him going into heaven."
verses.1:12: Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath day's journey away.
verses.1:13: And when they had entered, they went up to the upper room where they were staying: Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot and Judas son of James.
verses.1:14: All these were continually devoting themselves with one mind to prayer, along with women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers.
verses.1:15: And in these days Peter stood up in the midst of the brothers and said (and the crowd of persons together was about one hundred twenty),
verses.1:16: "Men and brothers, it was necessary for the Scripture to be fulfilled which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who became a guide to those who arrested Jesus,
verses.1:17: for he was numbered among us and obtained his allotted share in this ministry."
verses.1:18: (Now this man acquired a field with the wages of unrighteousness, and falling headlong, he burst open in the middle and all his inward parts spilled out.
verses.1:19: And it became known to all those dwelling in Jerusalem, so that in their own language that field was called Akeldama, that is, Field of Blood.)
verses.1:20: "For it is written in the Book of Psalms, 'Let his homestead become desolate, and let there be no one dwelling in it,' and, 'Let another take his office.'
verses.1:21: Therefore it is necessary that of the men who accompanied us during all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and went out among us,
verses.1:22: beginning from the baptism of John until the day on which He was taken up from us, one of these become a witness with us of His resurrection."
verses.1:23: And they put forward two: Joseph called Barsabbas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.
verses.1:24: And praying, they said, "You, Lord, who know the hearts of all, show which one of these two You have chosen
verses.1:25: to take the place of this ministry and apostleship from which Judas turned aside to go to his own place."
verses.1:26: And they cast lots for them, and the lot fell on Matthias, and he was numbered together with the eleven apostles.
verses.2:1: And when the day of Pentecost was being fulfilled, they were all together in one place.
verses.2:2: And suddenly a sound came out of heaven like that of a violent rushing wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
verses.2:3: And tongues as of fire appeared to them, dividing apart, and one rested upon each one of them.
verses.2:4: And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues, just as the Spirit was granting them to speak out.
verses.2:5: Now there were Jews residing in Jerusalem, devout men from every nation under heaven.
verses.2:6: And when this sound occurred, the multitude came together and was bewildered, because each one was hearing them speaking in his own language.
verses.2:7: And they were astonished and marveled, saying, "Look, are not all these who are speaking Galileans?
verses.2:8: And how is it that we each hear in our own language in which we were born?
verses.2:9: Parthians and Medes and Elamites, and those residing in Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,
verses.2:10: Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the regions of Libya around Cyrene, and visiting Romans,
verses.2:11: both Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabs—we hear them speaking in our own tongues the great deeds of God."
verses.2:12: And they were all astonished and thoroughly perplexed, saying to one another, "What does this mean?"
verses.2:13: But others, mocking, were saying, "They are full of sweet wine."
verses.2:14: But Peter, standing up with the eleven, raised his voice and spoke out to them: "Men of Judea and all who reside in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and give ear to my words.
verses.2:15: For these men are not drunk, as you suppose, for it is the third hour of the day;
verses.2:16: but this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:
verses.2:17: 'And it will be in the last days,' says God, 'I will pour out from My Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy, and your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams;
verses.2:18: and even upon My male slaves and upon My female slaves in those days I will pour out from My Spirit, and they will prophesy.
verses.2:19: And I will grant wonders in heaven above and signs on the earth below, blood and fire and vapor of smoke.
verses.2:20: The sun will be turned into darkness and the moon into blood, before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes.
verses.2:21: And it will be that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.'
verses.2:22: Men of Israel, listen to these words: Jesus the Nazarene, a man attested to you by God with mighty works and wonders and signs which God performed through Him in your midst, just as you yourselves know—
verses.2:23: this Man, delivered over by the predetermined purpose and foreknowledge of God, you nailed up by the hand of lawless men and put to death,
verses.2:24: whom God raised up, having loosed the pangs of death, because it was not possible for Him to be held fast by it.
verses.2:25: For David says concerning Him: 'I was continually seeing the Lord before me, because He is at my right hand, so that I may not be shaken.
verses.2:26: Therefore my heart was glad and my tongue exulted; moreover, my flesh also will dwell in hope;
verses.2:27: because You will not abandon my soul to Hades, nor will You allow Your Holy One to see decay.
verses.2:28: You have made known to me paths of life; You will fill me with gladness in Your presence.'
verses.2:29: Men and brothers, it is permissible to speak to you with boldness concerning the patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is among us to this day.
verses.2:30: Being a prophet, therefore, and knowing that God had sworn to him with an oath to seat one from the fruit of his loins upon his throne,
verses.2:31: having foreseen this, he spoke concerning the resurrection of the Christ, that He was neither abandoned to Hades, nor did His flesh see decay.
verses.2:32: This Jesus God raised up, of which we all are witnesses.
verses.2:33: Having been exalted, therefore, to the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, He has poured out this which you see and hear.
verses.2:34: For David did not ascend into the heavens, yet he himself says: 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at My right hand,
verses.2:35: until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet."'
verses.2:36: Therefore let all the house of Israel know with certainty that God has made Him both Lord and Christ—this Jesus whom you crucified."
verses.2:37: Now when they heard this, they were pierced to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, "What should we do, men and brothers?"
verses.2:38: And Peter said to them, "Repent, and each one of you must be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
verses.2:39: For the promise is for you and for your children and for all who are far off, as many as the Lord our God calls to Himself."
verses.2:40: And with many other words he testified solemnly and was urging them, saying, "Be saved from this crooked generation."
verses.2:41: So then, those who welcomed his word were baptized, and on that day about three thousand souls were added.
verses.2:42: And they were continually devoting themselves to the teaching of the apostles and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to the prayers.
verses.2:43: And fear was coming upon every soul, and many wonders and signs were taking place through the apostles.
verses.2:44: And all who had believed were together and held all things in common,
verses.2:45: and they were selling their properties and possessions and distributing them to all, as anyone had need.
verses.2:46: And day by day, continuing steadfastly with one mind in the temple and breaking bread from house to house, they were partaking of food with exultation and simplicity of heart,
verses.2:47: praising God and having favor with all the people. And day by day the Lord kept adding to their gathering those who were being saved.
verses.3:1: Now Peter and John were going up into the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.
verses.3:2: And a certain man, lame from his mother's womb, was being carried along, whom they placed daily at the gate of the temple called Beautiful to ask for alms from those entering into the temple.
verses.3:3: When he saw Peter and John about to enter into the temple, he asked to receive alms.
verses.3:4: And Peter, fixing his gaze on him along with John, said, "Look at us."
verses.3:5: So he gave them his attention, expecting to receive something from them.
verses.3:6: And Peter said, "Silver and gold I do not have, but what I do have, this I give to you: in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, walk!"
verses.3:7: And taking hold of him by the right hand, he raised him up; and immediately his feet and ankles were strengthened.
verses.3:8: And leaping up, he stood and began to walk, and he went with them into the temple, walking and leaping and praising God.
verses.3:9: And all the people saw him walking and praising God.
verses.3:10: And they recognized him as the one who used to sit for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, and they were filled with wonder and astonishment at what had happened to him.
verses.3:11: Now while he was clinging to Peter and John, all the people ran together to them at the portico called Solomon's, utterly amazed.
verses.3:12: When Peter saw this, he answered the people, "Men of Israel, why are you amazed at this, or why do you fix your gaze on us, as though by our own power or godliness we had made him walk?
verses.3:13: The God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified His Servant Jesus, whom you handed over and denied in the presence of Pilate, when he had decided to release Him.
verses.3:14: But you denied the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a murderer to be granted to you,
verses.3:15: and you put to death the Founder of life, whom God raised from the dead, of which we are witnesses.
verses.3:16: And on the basis of faith in His name, His name has strengthened this man whom you see and know; and the faith that is through Him has given him this complete health in the presence of all of you.
verses.3:17: And now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, just as your rulers also did.
verses.3:18: But what God announced beforehand through the mouth of all the prophets, that His Christ would suffer, He has fulfilled in this way.
verses.3:19: Repent therefore and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped away,
verses.3:20: so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and that He may send the Christ appointed for you, Jesus,
verses.3:21: whom heaven must receive until the times of the restoration of all things about which God spoke through the mouth of His holy prophets from ancient times.
verses.3:22: Moses indeed said, 'The Lord our God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers; you will listen to Him in everything that He may speak to you.
verses.3:23: And it will be that every soul who does not listen to that prophet will be utterly destroyed from among the people.'
verses.3:24: And indeed all the prophets from Samuel and those who came after, as many as have spoken, have also proclaimed these days.
verses.3:25: You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant which God made with your fathers, saying to Abraham, 'And in your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed.'
verses.3:26: To you first, God, having raised up His Servant, sent Him to bless you by turning each one away from your wicked ways."
verses.4:1: Now as they were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them,
verses.4:2: greatly disturbed because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
verses.4:3: And they laid hands on them and placed them in custody until the next day, for it was already evening.
verses.4:4: Yet many of those who had heard the word believed, and the number of the men came to be about five thousand.
verses.4:5: Now it happened on the next day that their rulers and elders and scribes were gathered together in Jerusalem,
verses.4:6: along with Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of high-priestly descent.
verses.4:7: And having set them in the center, they began to inquire, "By what power or in what name did you do this?"
verses.4:8: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, "Rulers of the people and elders,
verses.4:9: if we are being examined today regarding a good deed done to a sick man, as to how this man has been made well,
verses.4:10: let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead—by Him this man stands before you healthy.
verses.4:11: This One is the stone that was scorned by you, the builders, which has become the head of the corner.
verses.4:12: And in no one else is there salvation, for there is not another name under heaven that has been given among people by which we must be saved."
verses.4:13: Now as they observed the boldness of Peter and John and realized that they were uneducated and ordinary men, they were amazed; and they recognized that they had been with Jesus.
verses.4:14: And seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they had nothing to say in reply.
verses.4:15: So having ordered them to leave the Sanhedrin, they began conferring with one another,
verses.4:16: saying, "What should we do with these men? For that a notable sign has taken place through them is evident to all who live in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.
verses.4:17: Yet so that it may not spread any further among the people, let us threaten them to speak no longer in this name to anyone."
verses.4:18: And having called them in, they commanded them not to speak or to teach at all in the name of Jesus.
verses.4:19: But Peter and John answered and said to them, "Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, you judge;
verses.4:20: for we cannot refrain from speaking about the things we have seen and heard."
verses.4:21: And after threatening them further, they released them, finding no way to punish them because of the people, since everyone was glorifying God for what had happened;
verses.4:22: for the man on whom this sign of healing had taken place was more than forty years old.
verses.4:23: When they had been released, they went to their own people and reported everything that the chief priests and the elders had said to them.
verses.4:24: And when they heard this, they lifted up their voice with one accord to God and said, "Sovereign Master, You are the One who made heaven and earth and the sea and all that is in them,
verses.4:25: who by the Holy Spirit, through the mouth of our father David Your servant, said, 'Why did the nations rage and the peoples devise empty things?
verses.4:26: The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers were gathered together as one against the Lord and against His Christ.'
verses.4:27: For truly in this city there were gathered together against Your holy Servant Jesus, whom You anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, along with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel,
verses.4:28: to do whatever Your hand and Your purpose determined beforehand to take place.
verses.4:29: And now, Lord, look upon their threats, and grant to Your slaves to speak Your word with all boldness,
verses.4:30: while You stretch out Your hand for healing, and signs and wonders take place through the name of Your holy Servant Jesus."
verses.4:31: And when they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered together was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began speaking the word of God with boldness.
verses.4:32: Now the multitude of those who had believed was of one heart and soul, and not a single one claimed that any of his possessions was his own, but everything was held in common among them.
verses.4:33: And with great power the apostles were bearing testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon them all.
verses.4:34: For there was not even a needy person among them, because as many as were owners of lands or houses would sell them and bring the proceeds of what was being sold
verses.4:35: and lay them at the feet of the apostles; and distribution was made to each one according as anyone had need.
verses.4:36: Now Joseph, who was called Barnabas by the apostles (which translated means Son of Encouragement), a Levite, a native of Cyprus,
verses.4:37: owning a field, sold it, brought the money, and laid it at the feet of the apostles.
verses.5:1: Now a certain man named Ananias, together with his wife Sapphira, sold a piece of property,
verses.5:2: and kept back some of the proceeds, with his wife also knowing about it, and bringing a certain part, he placed it at the feet of the apostles.
verses.5:3: But Peter said, "Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart for you to lie to the Holy Spirit and keep back some of the proceeds of the field?
verses.5:4: While it remained, did it not remain yours, and after it was sold, was it not under your authority? Why is it that you put this deed in your heart? You did not lie to people, but to God."
verses.5:5: And as Ananias heard these words, he fell down and breathed his last; and great fear came upon all who heard.
verses.5:6: Then the younger men rose up, wrapped him up, and carrying him out, they buried him.
verses.5:7: Now an interval of about three hours passed, and his wife, not knowing what had happened, came in.
verses.5:8: And Peter responded to her, "Tell me, did you sell the field for this much?" And she said, "Yes, for that much."
verses.5:9: Then Peter said to her, "Why is it that you agreed together to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out."
verses.5:10: And immediately she fell at his feet and breathed her last; and when the young men came in, they found her dead, and carrying her out, they buried her beside her husband.
verses.5:11: And great fear came upon the whole church and upon all who heard these things.
verses.5:12: Now through the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were taking place among the people; and they were all with one accord in Solomon's Portico.
verses.5:13: Yet none of the rest dared to join themselves to them, but the people held them in high esteem,
verses.5:14: and even more, believers in the Lord were being added, multitudes of both men and women;
verses.5:15: so that they even carried the sick out into the streets and placed them on cots and mats, in order that as Peter came by, at least his shadow might overshadow some of them.
verses.5:16: And the multitude from the cities around Jerusalem was also gathering together, bringing the sick and those troubled by unclean spirits, who were all being healed.
verses.5:17: But the high priest rose up, along with all those with him—that is, the sect of the Sadducees—and they were filled with jealousy,
verses.5:18: and they laid hands on the apostles and put them in public custody.
verses.5:19: But an angel of the Lord during the night opened the doors of the prison, and leading them out, said,
verses.5:20: "Go, and taking your stand in the temple, speak to the people all the words of this life."
verses.5:21: And when they heard this, they entered the temple at daybreak and began teaching. Now when the high priest and those with him arrived, they summoned the Sanhedrin and the entire council of elders of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison to have them brought.
verses.5:22: But the officers who arrived did not find them in the prison, and returning, they reported,
verses.5:23: saying, "We found the prison locked with complete security and the guards standing at the doors, but when we opened them, we found no one inside."
verses.5:24: Now when both the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were greatly perplexed about them as to what this might come to.
verses.5:25: Then someone came and reported to them, "Look, the men whom you put in the prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people."
verses.5:26: Then the captain went with the officers and brought them, without force, for they were afraid of the people, that they might be stoned.
verses.5:27: And when they had brought them, they set them before the Sanhedrin. And the high priest questioned them,
verses.5:28: saying, "We strictly ordered you not to teach in this name, and look, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you intend to bring this man's blood upon us."
verses.5:29: But Peter and the apostles answered and said, "We must obey God rather than people.
verses.5:30: The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you put to death by hanging Him on a tree.
verses.5:31: Him God exalted to His right hand as Leader and Savior, to grant repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.
verses.5:32: And we are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey Him."
verses.5:33: Now when they heard this, they were infuriated and wanted to put them to death.
verses.5:34: But a certain Pharisee in the Sanhedrin named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law respected by all the people, stood up and ordered the men to be put outside for a short time,
verses.5:35: and he said to them, "Men of Israel, take care for yourselves regarding these men, what you are about to do.
verses.5:36: For before these days Theudas rose up, claiming himself to be somebody, and a number of men, about four hundred, joined him; he was killed, and all who followed him were dispersed and came to nothing.
verses.5:37: After him Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census and drew away people after himself; he too perished, and all who followed him were scattered.
verses.5:38: And now I say to you, stay away from these men and let them alone (for if this plan or this work is from men, it will be overthrown,
verses.5:39: but if it is from God, you will not be able to overthrow them), or else you may even be found fighting against God." And they were persuaded by him,
verses.5:40: and after calling the apostles in and flogging them, they ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released them.
verses.5:41: So they went on their way from the presence of the Sanhedrin, rejoicing that they were considered worthy to be dishonored for the sake of the Name.
verses.5:42: And every day, in the temple and from house to house, they did not cease teaching and proclaiming the good news of Jesus as the Christ.
verses.6:1: Now in these days, as the disciples were increasing in number, a complaint arose from the Hellenists against the Hebrews because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution.
verses.6:2: So the twelve summoned the multitude of the disciples and said, "It is not fitting for us to leave the word of God in order to serve tables.
verses.6:3: But, brothers, select from among you seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we will appoint over this duty;
verses.6:4: while we will devote ourselves continually to prayer and to the ministry of the word."
verses.6:5: And this statement pleased the whole multitude, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte from Antioch,
verses.6:6: whom they presented before the apostles; and after praying, they laid their hands on them.
verses.6:7: And the word of God kept growing, and the number of the disciples in Jerusalem was multiplying greatly, and a large crowd of the priests was becoming obedient to the faith.
verses.6:8: Now Stephen, full of grace and power, was performing great wonders and signs among the people.
verses.6:9: But some men rose up from what was called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, and of the Cyrenians and Alexandrians, and some of those from Cilicia and Asia, disputing with Stephen.
verses.6:10: Yet they were not able to withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by whom he was speaking.
verses.6:11: Then they secretly instigated men who said, "We have heard him speaking blasphemous words against Moses and God."
verses.6:12: And they stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes, and coming upon him, they seized him and brought him to the Sanhedrin.
verses.6:13: And they put forward false witnesses who said, "This man never stops speaking words against the holy place and the law,
verses.6:14: for we have heard him saying that this Jesus the Nazarene will destroy this place and will change the customs that Moses handed down to us."
verses.6:15: And all who were sitting in the Sanhedrin, gazing intently at him, saw his face like the face of an angel.
verses.7:1: Then the high priest said, "Are these matters so?"
verses.7:2: And he said, "Men, brothers and fathers, listen! The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran,
verses.7:3: and said to him, 'Go out from your land and from your relatives, and come into the land that I will show you.'
verses.7:4: Then he went out from the land of the Chaldeans and lived in Haran. And from there, after his father died, He relocated him into this land in which you now live,
verses.7:5: and He did not give him an inheritance in it, not even the space of a foot; yet He promised to give it to him as a possession and to his offspring after him, even though he had no child.
verses.7:6: And God spoke in this way, that his offspring would be resident aliens in a foreign land, and they would enslave them and mistreat them for four hundred years.
verses.7:7: 'And the nation to which they will be enslaved I Myself will judge,' God said, 'and after these things they will come out and worship Me in this place.'
verses.7:8: And He gave him the covenant of circumcision; and so he fathered Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob fathered the twelve patriarchs.
verses.7:9: And the patriarchs, being jealous of Joseph, sold him into Egypt; yet God was with him,
verses.7:10: and rescued him from all his afflictions, and gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, king of Egypt; and he appointed him ruler over Egypt and all his household.
verses.7:11: Now a famine came over all Egypt and Canaan, and great affliction, and our fathers could not find food.
verses.7:12: But when Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent out our fathers the first time.
verses.7:13: And on the second visit Joseph was made known to his brothers, and Joseph's family became known to Pharaoh.
verses.7:14: Then Joseph sent and summoned his father Jacob and all his relatives, seventy-five persons in all.
verses.7:15: And Jacob went down to Egypt. And he and our fathers died,
verses.7:16: and they were carried over to Shechem and laid in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
verses.7:17: But as the time of the promise that God had pledged to Abraham was drawing near, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
verses.7:18: until another king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
verses.7:19: This man dealt craftily with our race and mistreated our fathers, making them expose their infants so that they would not be kept alive.
verses.7:20: At that time Moses was born, and he was beautiful to God; and he was brought up for three months in his father's house.
verses.7:21: And when he had been exposed, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and brought him up for herself as a son.
verses.7:22: And Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was powerful in his words and deeds.
verses.7:23: Now when a forty-year period was coming to completion for him, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the sons of Israel.
verses.7:24: And seeing one of them being wronged, he defended him and avenged the oppressed man by striking down the Egyptian.
verses.7:25: And he supposed that his brothers understood that God was giving them deliverance through his hand, but they did not understand.
verses.7:26: And on the following day he appeared to them as they were fighting and tried to reconcile them to peace, saying, 'Men, you are brothers; why are you wronging one another?'
verses.7:27: But the one who was wronging his neighbor pushed him away, saying, 'Who appointed you ruler and judge over us?
verses.7:28: Do you want to kill me in the same way you killed the Egyptian yesterday?'
verses.7:29: And at this word Moses fled and became a resident alien in the land of Midian, where he fathered two sons.
verses.7:30: And when forty years had been completed, an angel appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in a flame of fire in a bush.
verses.7:31: When Moses saw it, he marveled at the sight; and as he was approaching to look closely, the voice of the Lord came:
verses.7:32: 'I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.' And trembling, Moses did not dare to look closely.
verses.7:33: And the Lord said to him, 'Untie the sandals from your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.
verses.7:34: I have surely seen the mistreatment of My people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to rescue them. And now come, I will send you to Egypt.'
verses.7:35: This Moses, whom they disowned, saying, 'Who appointed you ruler and judge?'—this man God has sent as both ruler and redeemer by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
verses.7:36: This man led them out, performing wonders and signs in the land of Egypt and in the Red Sea and in the wilderness for forty years.
verses.7:37: This is the Moses who said to the sons of Israel, 'God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers like me.'
verses.7:38: This is the one who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers—the one who received living oracles to give to you,
verses.7:39: to whom our fathers were unwilling to be obedient, but they pushed him away and in their hearts turned back to Egypt,
verses.7:40: saying to Aaron, 'Make for us gods who will go before us; for this Moses, who led us out of the land of Egypt—we do not know what has happened to him.'
verses.7:41: And they made a calf in those days and brought a sacrifice to the idol, and were rejoicing in the works of their hands.
verses.7:42: But God turned away and gave them over to worship the host of heaven, just as it is written in the book of the prophets: 'Did you offer to Me slaughtered animals and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?
verses.7:43: And you took up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of the god Rompha, the images that you made to bow down to them; and I will relocate you beyond Babylon.'
verses.7:44: Our fathers had the tabernacle of testimony in the wilderness, just as the One who spoke to Moses directed him to make it according to the pattern that he had seen,
verses.7:45: which our fathers also, having received it in turn, brought in with Joshua when taking possession of the nations that God drove out from before our fathers, until the days of David,
verses.7:46: who found favor before God and asked to find a dwelling place for the house of Jacob.
verses.7:47: But Solomon built a house for Him.
verses.7:48: Yet the Most High does not live in things made by hands, just as the prophet says:
verses.7:49: 'Heaven is My throne, and the earth is the footstool of My feet; what kind of house will you build for Me,' says the Lord, 'or what is the place of My rest?
verses.7:50: Did not My hand make all these things?'
verses.7:51: Stiff-necked and uncircumcised in hearts and ears, you are always resisting the Holy Spirit; as your fathers did, so also do you.
verses.7:52: Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those who announced beforehand the coming of the Righteous One, of whom you have now become betrayers and murderers,
verses.7:53: you who received the law by the ordinances of angels, and did not keep it."
verses.7:54: Now as they heard these things, they were cut to their hearts, and they were gnashing their teeth at him.
verses.7:55: But being full of the Holy Spirit, he gazed intently into heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God,
verses.7:56: and he said, "Look, I see the heavens opened up and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God."
verses.7:57: But crying out with a loud voice, they covered their ears and rushed upon him with one accord,
verses.7:58: and having driven him out of the city, they began stoning him. And the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
verses.7:59: And they were stoning Stephen as he was calling out and saying, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."
verses.7:60: And kneeling down, he cried out with a loud voice, "Lord, do not charge this sin against them." And when he had said this, he fell asleep.
verses.8:1: Now Saul was approving of his execution. And on that day a great persecution arose against the church in Jerusalem, and all were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.
verses.8:2: Devout men buried Stephen and made great lamentation over him.
verses.8:3: Saul, however, was ravaging the church, entering house after house; and dragging off both men and women, he was delivering them into prison.
verses.8:4: Therefore those who had been scattered went about preaching the good news of the word.
verses.8:5: Philip went down to the city of Samaria and was proclaiming the Christ to them.
verses.8:6: And the crowds with one accord were paying attention to the things spoken by Philip as they heard and saw the signs that he was performing.
verses.8:7: For unclean spirits were coming out of many of those who had them, crying out with a loud voice; and many who were paralyzed and lame were healed.
verses.8:8: And there was much joy in that city.
verses.8:9: Now a certain man named Simon had previously been in the city, practicing magic and astonishing the nation of Samaria, saying that he himself was someone great,
verses.8:10: to whom all, from the least to the greatest, were paying attention, saying, "This man is the Power of God that is called Great."
verses.8:11: And they were paying attention to him because for a considerable time he had astonished them with his magic arts.
verses.8:12: But when they believed Philip as he was preaching the good news about the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were being baptized, both men and women.
verses.8:13: And Simon himself also believed; and having been baptized, he was continuing closely with Philip, and as he observed signs and great works of power taking place, he was astonished.
verses.8:14: Now when the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them,
verses.8:15: who came down and prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit.
verses.8:16: For He had not yet fallen upon any of them; they had only been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.8:17: Then they were laying their hands on them, and they were receiving the Holy Spirit.
verses.8:18: Now when Simon saw that through the laying on of the apostles' hands the Spirit was given, he offered them money,
verses.8:19: saying, "Give me also this authority, so that anyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit."
verses.8:20: But Peter said to him, "May your silver go to destruction with you, because you thought to acquire the gift of God through money!
verses.8:21: You have no part or lot in this matter, for your heart is not right before God.
verses.8:22: Therefore repent of this wickedness of yours, and plead with the Lord, if perhaps the intent of your heart may be forgiven you;
verses.8:23: for I see that you are in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of unrighteousness."
verses.8:24: And Simon answered and said, "Plead with the Lord yourselves on my behalf, so that nothing of the things you have spoken may come upon me."
verses.8:25: So when they had solemnly testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they were returning to Jerusalem and were preaching the good news to many villages of the Samaritans.
verses.8:26: Now an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, "Rise and go toward the south to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza." This is deserted.
verses.8:27: So he rose and went; and look, an Ethiopian man, a eunuch, a high official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was in charge of all her treasury—he had come to Jerusalem to worship,
verses.8:28: and he was returning and sitting in his chariot, and he was reading the prophet Isaiah.
verses.8:29: Then the Spirit said to Philip, "Go over and join this chariot."
verses.8:30: So Philip ran up and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and he said, "Do you really understand what you are reading?"
verses.8:31: And he said, "How indeed could I, unless someone guides me?" And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
verses.8:32: Now the passage of Scripture that he was reading was this: "Like a sheep He was led to slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer, so He does not open His mouth.
verses.8:33: In humiliation His justice was taken away; who will describe His generation? For His life is taken away from the earth."
verses.8:34: And the eunuch answered Philip and said, "Please, I ask you, about whom does the prophet say this—about himself or about someone else?"
verses.8:35: Then Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture, he preached to him the good news of Jesus.
verses.8:36: And as they were going along the road, they came to some water; and the eunuch said, "Look, water! What prevents me from being baptized?"
verses.8:38: And he ordered the chariot to stop; and they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.
verses.8:39: And when they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord snatched Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no longer, for he went on his way rejoicing.
verses.8:40: But Philip was found at Azotus; and as he passed through, he was preaching the good news to all the cities until he came to Caesarea.
verses.9:1: Now Saul, still breathing threats and murder against the disciples of the Lord, approached the high priest
verses.9:2: and requested from him letters for Damascus to the synagogues, so that if he found any who were of the Way, both men and women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.
verses.9:3: And as he was traveling, it happened that he drew near to Damascus, and suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him;
verses.9:4: and falling to the ground, he heard a voice saying to him, "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?"
verses.9:5: And he said, "Who are You, Lord?" And He said, "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
verses.9:6: But rise and enter the city, and it will be told to you what you must do."
verses.9:7: Now the men who were traveling with him stood speechless, hearing the voice, yet seeing no one.
verses.9:8: And Saul got up from the ground, and though his eyes were open, he saw nothing; so leading him by the hand, they brought him into Damascus.
verses.9:9: And for three days he was without sight, and he neither ate nor drank.
verses.9:10: Now there was a certain disciple in Damascus named Ananias, and the Lord said to him in a vision, "Ananias." And he said, "Here I am, Lord."
verses.9:11: And the Lord said to him, "Rise and go to the street called Straight, and inquire at the house of Judas for a man from Tarsus named Saul; for look, he is praying,
verses.9:12: and in a vision he has seen a man named Ananias coming in and laying hands on him so that he might regain his sight."
verses.9:13: But Ananias answered, "Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much harm he has done to Your saints in Jerusalem;
verses.9:14: and here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on Your name."
verses.9:15: But the Lord said to him, "Go, for this man is a chosen vessel of Mine to carry My name before Gentiles and kings and the sons of Israel;
verses.9:16: for I will show him how much he must suffer for the sake of My name."
verses.9:17: So Ananias departed and entered the house, and laying his hands on him, he said, "Brother Saul, the Lord has sent me, Jesus who appeared to you on the road by which you were coming, so that you may regain your sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit."
verses.9:18: And immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he regained his sight; and getting up, he was baptized,
verses.9:19: and having taken food, he was strengthened. Now he was with the disciples in Damascus for some days,
verses.9:20: and immediately in the synagogues he began proclaiming Jesus, that He is the Son of God.
verses.9:21: And all who were hearing him were amazed and kept saying, "Is this not the man who ravaged in Jerusalem those who call on this name, and who had come here for this purpose, to bring them bound before the chief priests?"
verses.9:22: But Saul kept growing all the more in strength and was confounding the Jews living in Damascus by proving that this One is the Christ.
verses.9:23: When many days had elapsed, the Jews plotted together to kill him,
verses.9:24: but their plot became known to Saul. They were also closely watching the gates both day and night so that they might kill him;
verses.9:25: but his disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.
verses.9:26: When he arrived in Jerusalem, he kept trying to associate with the disciples; and they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.
verses.9:27: But Barnabas took hold of him and brought him to the apostles, and recounted to them how on the road he had seen the Lord, and that He had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had spoken boldly in the name of Jesus.
verses.9:28: And he was with them, going in and going out in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord,
verses.9:29: and he was speaking and disputing with the Hellenists, but they were attempting to kill him.
verses.9:30: When the brothers learned of this, they brought him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
verses.9:31: So the church throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, being built up; and walking in the fear of the Lord and in the encouragement of the Holy Spirit, it continued to multiply.
verses.9:32: Now it happened that as Peter was traveling through all parts, he came down also to the saints living in Lydda.
verses.9:33: There he found a certain man named Aeneas, lying on a mat for eight years, who was paralyzed.
verses.9:34: And Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you; rise and make your bed." And immediately he got up.
verses.9:35: And all who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
verses.9:36: Now in Joppa there was a certain female disciple named Tabitha, which translated means Dorcas; she was full of good works and acts of charity that she continually did.
verses.9:37: And it happened in those days that she became sick and died; and when they had washed her, they laid her in an upper room.
verses.9:38: Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, urging him, "Do not delay in coming over to us."
verses.9:39: So Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, they brought him up to the upper room; and all the widows stood beside him weeping and showing the tunics and garments that Dorcas used to make while she was with them.
verses.9:40: But Peter sent them all outside, and kneeling down, he prayed; and turning toward the body, he said, "Tabitha, rise." And she opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, she sat up.
verses.9:41: And giving her his hand, he raised her up; and calling the saints and the widows, he presented her alive.
verses.9:42: And it became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.
verses.9:43: And it happened that he stayed many days in Joppa with a certain Simon, a tanner.
verses.10:1: Now a certain man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion of the cohort called the Italian,
verses.10:2: devout and fearing God with all his household, doing many acts of charity for the people and praying to God continually,
verses.10:3: saw clearly in a vision, about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God coming in to him and saying to him, "Cornelius."
verses.10:4: And fixing his eyes on him and becoming frightened, he said, "What is it, sir?" And he said to him, "Your prayers and your acts of charity have ascended for a memorial before God.
verses.10:5: And now send men to Joppa and send for a certain Simon who is called Peter;
verses.10:6: he is lodging with a certain Simon, a tanner, whose house is by the sea."
verses.10:7: Now when the angel who was speaking to him departed, calling two of the household servants and a devout soldier from those who attended him,
verses.10:8: and explaining everything to them, he sent them to Joppa.
verses.10:9: On the next day, while they were traveling and approaching the city, Peter went up onto the housetop to pray about the sixth hour.
verses.10:10: And he became very hungry and wanted to eat; but while they were making preparations, a trance came upon him,
verses.10:11: and he sees heaven opened and a certain object like a large sheet descending, being lowered by four corners onto the earth,
verses.10:12: in which were all the four-footed animals and crawling creatures of the earth and birds of the sky.
verses.10:13: And a voice came to him, "Get up, Peter; slaughter and eat."
verses.10:14: But Peter said, "By no means, Lord, because I have never eaten anything common and unclean."
verses.10:15: And a voice came to him again a second time, "What God has cleansed, you must not regard as common."
verses.10:16: Now this happened three times, and immediately the object was taken up into heaven.
verses.10:17: Now while Peter was greatly perplexed within himself about what the vision that he had seen might mean, look, the men who had been sent by Cornelius, having inquired for Simon's house, stood at the gate,
verses.10:18: and calling out, they were asking whether Simon, who is called Peter, was lodging there.
verses.10:19: While Peter was reflecting on the vision, the Spirit said to him, "Look, men are looking for you.
verses.10:20: But get up, go down, and travel with them without hesitating at all, because I have sent them."
verses.10:21: So Peter went down to the men and said, "Look, I am the one you are looking for. What is the reason why you are here?"
verses.10:22: And they said, "Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man and fearing God, and well spoken of by the whole nation of the Jews, was divinely directed by a holy angel to send for you to his house and to hear words from you."
verses.10:23: So he invited them in and lodged them. On the next day he got up and went out with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa went along with him.
verses.10:24: And on the next day he entered Caesarea. Now Cornelius was expecting them, having called together his relatives and close friends.
verses.10:25: And when it happened that Peter entered, Cornelius met him, fell at his feet, and bowed down in worship.
verses.10:26: But Peter raised him up, saying, "Stand up; I myself am also a man."
verses.10:27: And conversing with him, he went inside and found many who had gathered together,
verses.10:28: and he said to them, "You yourselves know how unlawful it is for a Jewish man to associate with or to visit a foreigner; yet God has shown me to call no person common or unclean.
verses.10:29: Therefore I also came without objection when I was sent for. So I ask for what reason you have sent for me."
verses.10:30: And Cornelius said, "Four days ago to this very hour, I was praying at the ninth hour in my house, and look, a man stood before me in shining clothing
verses.10:31: and said, 'Cornelius, your prayer has been heard and your acts of charity have been remembered before God.
verses.10:32: Therefore send to Joppa and summon Simon, who is called Peter; he is lodging in the house of Simon, a tanner, by the sea.'
verses.10:33: So I sent for you at once, and you have done well in coming. Now then, we are all present before God to hear all the things that have been commanded to you by the Lord."
verses.10:34: Then Peter opened his mouth and said, "In truth I comprehend that God is not one who shows partiality,
verses.10:35: but in every nation the one who fears Him and practices righteousness is acceptable to Him.
verses.10:36: The word that He sent to the sons of Israel, proclaiming good news of peace through Jesus Christ—He is Lord of all—
verses.10:37: you yourselves know the event that took place throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee after the baptism that John proclaimed:
verses.10:38: Jesus from Nazareth, how God anointed Him with the Holy Spirit and power, who went around doing good and healing all those oppressed by the devil, because God was with Him.
verses.10:39: And we are witnesses of all the things that He did both in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They also put Him to death by hanging Him on a tree.
verses.10:40: This One God raised on the third day and granted Him to become visible,
verses.10:41: not to all the people, but to witnesses who had been chosen beforehand by God, to us, who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.
verses.10:42: And He commanded us to proclaim to the people and to testify solemnly that He is the One who has been appointed by God as Judge of the living and the dead.
verses.10:43: To Him all the prophets testify that everyone believing in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name."
verses.10:44: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all those who were listening to the word.
verses.10:45: And the believers from the circumcision, as many as had come with Peter, were amazed that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles;
verses.10:46: for they were hearing them speaking in tongues and magnifying God. Then Peter responded,
verses.10:47: "Can anyone withhold the water so that these should not be baptized, who received the Holy Spirit just as we also did?"
verses.10:48: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay for some days.
verses.11:1: Now the apostles and the brothers who were throughout Judea heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.
verses.11:2: And when Peter went up to Jerusalem, those of the circumcision disputed with him,
verses.11:3: saying, "You went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them."
verses.11:4: But Peter began and laid it out for them in order, saying,
verses.11:5: "I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: a certain object descending, like a large sheet being lowered from heaven by four corners, and it came all the way to me.
verses.11:6: Gazing intently into it, I examined it and saw the four-footed animals of the earth, and the wild beasts, and the crawling creatures, and the birds of the sky.
verses.11:7: I also heard a voice saying to me, 'Get up, Peter; slaughter and eat.'
verses.11:8: But I said, 'By no means, Lord, because nothing common or unclean has ever entered my mouth.'
verses.11:9: But a voice answered a second time from heaven, 'What God has cleansed, you must not regard as common.'
verses.11:10: Now this happened three times, and everything was drawn up again into heaven.
verses.11:11: And look, at that very moment three men arrived at the house in which we were, having been sent from Caesarea to me.
verses.11:12: And the Spirit told me to go with them, making no distinction. These six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man's house.
verses.11:13: And he reported to us how he had seen the angel standing in his house and saying, 'Send to Joppa and summon Simon, who is called Peter,
verses.11:14: who will speak words to you by which you will be saved, you and all your household.'
verses.11:15: And as I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them just as He also did upon us at the beginning.
verses.11:16: And I remembered the word of the Lord, how He said, 'John indeed baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.'
verses.11:17: Therefore, if God gave to them the same gift as also to us who believed on the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to be able to hinder God?"
verses.11:18: When they heard these things, they fell silent and glorified God, saying, "Then to the Gentiles also God has granted repentance leading to life."
verses.11:19: Now those who were scattered because of the affliction that arose over Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia and Cyprus and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except Jews alone.
verses.11:20: But there were some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who on coming to Antioch spoke to the Hellenists also, proclaiming the good news of the Lord Jesus.
verses.11:21: And the hand of the Lord was with them, and a large number who believed turned to the Lord.
verses.11:22: And the report concerning them reached the ears of the church that was in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas out as far as Antioch.
verses.11:23: When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced and exhorted them all with purpose of heart to remain faithful to the Lord,
verses.11:24: for he was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And a considerable crowd was added to the Lord.
verses.11:25: Then he departed for Tarsus to search for Saul,
verses.11:26: and when he found him, he brought him to Antioch. And it happened that for an entire year they met together in the church and taught a considerable crowd, and in Antioch the disciples were first called Christians.
verses.11:27: Now in these days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
verses.11:28: And one of them named Agabus stood up and indicated through the Spirit that a great famine was about to occur over the whole inhabited world, which took place under Claudius.
verses.11:29: And according to each one's means, the disciples determined, every one of them, to send relief to the brothers living in Judea;
verses.11:30: and this they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.
verses.12:1: Now at that time Herod the king laid hands on some of those belonging to the church to mistreat them.
verses.12:2: And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.
verses.12:3: And seeing that it was pleasing to the Jews, he proceeded to arrest Peter also (now these were the days of Unleavened Bread),
verses.12:4: and having seized him, he put him in prison, handing him over to four squads of four soldiers to guard him, intending after the Passover to bring him out before the people.
verses.12:5: So Peter was kept in the prison, but prayer was being made earnestly by the church to God for him.
verses.12:6: Now when Herod was about to bring him forward, on that night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and guards in front of the door were guarding the prison.
verses.12:7: And look, an angel of the Lord stood there, and a light shone in the cell; and striking Peter's side, he roused him, saying, "Get up quickly!" And his chains fell off his hands.
verses.12:8: And the angel said to him, "Fasten your belt and tie on your sandals." And he did so. Then he said to him, "Wrap your cloak around you and follow me."
verses.12:9: And he went out and was following him, and he did not know that what was happening through the angel was real, but supposed he was seeing a vision.
verses.12:10: When they had passed the first and second guard posts, they came to the iron gate that leads into the city, which opened for them by itself; and going out, they went along one street, and immediately the angel departed from him.
verses.12:11: And when Peter came to himself, he said, "Now I truly know that the Lord has sent out His angel and rescued me from the hand of Herod and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews."
verses.12:12: And when he realized this, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was called Mark, where a considerable number were gathered together and praying.
verses.12:13: When he knocked at the door of the gate, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer.
verses.12:14: And recognizing Peter's voice, out of joy she did not open the gate, but ran inside and reported that Peter was standing in front of the gate.
verses.12:15: They said to her, "You are out of your mind!" But she kept insisting that it was so. And they kept saying, "It is his angel."
verses.12:16: Meanwhile Peter kept on knocking; and when they opened it, they saw him and were astounded.
verses.12:17: Motioning to them with his hand to be silent, he described to them how the Lord had led him out of the prison. And he said, "Report these things to James and to the brothers." Then he went out and departed to another place.
verses.12:18: Now when day came, there was no small commotion among the soldiers as to what had become of Peter.
verses.12:19: And when Herod had searched for him and did not find him, he examined the guards and ordered them to be led away. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.
verses.12:20: Now he was bitterly angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon; and with one accord they came before him, and having won over Blastus, the one in charge of the king's bedchamber, they were asking for peace, because their country was supplied with food from the king's territory.
verses.12:21: On an appointed day, Herod put on royal attire, took his seat on the tribunal, and began delivering a public address to them.
verses.12:22: And the populace kept shouting, "The voice of a god, and not of a man!"
verses.12:23: And immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he did not give the glory to God; and having been eaten by worms, he breathed his last.
verses.12:24: But the word of God kept growing and multiplying.
verses.12:25: Now Barnabas and Saul returned, having completed the service to Jerusalem, bringing along with them John, who was called Mark.
verses.13:1: Now in Antioch, in the church that was there, there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, and Simeon who was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, who was raised with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
verses.13:2: While they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart now for Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them."
verses.13:3: Then, after fasting and praying and laying their hands on them, they sent them off.
verses.13:4: So, having been sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia, and from there they sailed away to Cyprus.
verses.13:5: When they arrived in Salamis, they were proclaiming the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews; and they also had John as an assistant.
verses.13:6: When they had gone through the entire island as far as Paphos, they found a certain man, a magician and Jewish false prophet whose name was Bar-Jesus,
verses.13:7: who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. This man summoned Barnabas and Saul and sought to hear the word of God.
verses.13:8: But Elymas the magician (for that is how his name is translated) was opposing them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.
verses.13:9: But Saul, who was also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fixed his gaze on him
verses.13:10: and said, "You who are full of all deceit and all villainy, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness, will you not stop twisting the straight ways of the Lord?
verses.13:11: And now, look, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a time." Immediately a mist and darkness fell upon him, and going about, he began searching for people to lead him by the hand.
verses.13:12: Then the proconsul, seeing what had happened, believed, being astounded at the teaching of the Lord.
verses.13:13: Now setting sail from Paphos, Paul and his companions came to Perga in Pamphylia; but John departed from them and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.13:14: But they went on from Perga and arrived at Pisidian Antioch; and going into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, they sat down.
verses.13:15: After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue rulers sent word to them, saying, "Brothers, if you have any word of encouragement for the people, speak."
verses.13:16: So Paul stood up, and motioning with his hand, he said, "Men of Israel and you who fear God, listen.
verses.13:17: The God of this people Israel chose our fathers, and He made the people great during their stay as foreigners in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm He led them out of it.
verses.13:18: And for a period of about forty years He put up with them in the wilderness.
verses.13:19: And after destroying seven nations in the land of Canaan, He gave their land to them as an inheritance
verses.13:20: in about four hundred and fifty years. And after these things He gave judges until Samuel the prophet.
verses.13:21: Then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul the son of Kish, a man from the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.
verses.13:22: And after removing him, He raised up David for them as king, concerning whom He also testified and said, 'I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after My heart, who will do all My will.'
verses.13:23: From this man's offspring God, according to promise, brought to Israel a Savior, Jesus,
verses.13:24: after John had proclaimed beforehand, ahead of His coming, a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
verses.13:25: And as John was completing his course, he kept saying, 'What do you suppose me to be? I am not He; rather, look, One is coming after me, the sandal of whose feet I am not worthy to untie.'
verses.13:26: Brothers, sons of the family of Abraham, and those among you who fear God, to us the word of this salvation has been sent.
verses.13:27: For those living in Jerusalem and their rulers, failing to recognize Him or the voices of the prophets that are read every Sabbath, fulfilled them by condemning Him.
verses.13:28: And though they found no grounds for death, they asked Pilate that He be put to death.
verses.13:29: And when they had carried out all the things written concerning Him, they took Him down from the tree and laid Him in a tomb.
verses.13:30: But God raised Him from the dead;
verses.13:31: and for many days He appeared to those who had gone up with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now His witnesses to the people.
verses.13:32: And we bring you the good news about the promise made to the fathers,
verses.13:33: that God has completely fulfilled it for our children by raising up Jesus, just as it is also written in the second Psalm: 'You are My Son; today I have fathered You.'
verses.13:34: And as for the fact that He raised Him from the dead, no longer about to return to decay, He has spoken in this way: 'I will give you the holy and faithful blessings of David.'
verses.13:35: Therefore He also says in another place, 'You will not allow Your Holy One to see decay.'
verses.13:36: For David, after serving the purpose of God in his own generation, fell asleep and was added to his fathers and saw decay;
verses.13:37: but the One whom God raised did not see decay.
verses.13:38: Therefore let it be known to you, brothers, that through Him forgiveness of sins is being proclaimed to you, and from everything from which you could not be justified in the law of Moses,
verses.13:39: in Him everyone who believes is justified.
verses.13:40: Watch out, then, so that what was spoken in the prophets may not come about:
verses.13:41: 'Look, you scoffers, and be amazed, and perish; for I am doing a work in your days, a work that you will never believe even if someone recounts it to you in full.'"
verses.13:42: As they were going out, the people were urging that these words be spoken to them on the next Sabbath.
verses.13:43: And when the synagogue assembly broke up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, who, speaking with them, were urging them to remain in the grace of God.
verses.13:44: On the next Sabbath nearly the whole city gathered together to hear the word of God.
verses.13:45: But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy and began contradicting the things being spoken by Paul, speaking abusively.
verses.13:46: Then Paul and Barnabas spoke out boldly and said, "It was necessary for the word of God to be spoken to you first; since you push it away and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, look, we are turning to the Gentiles.
verses.13:47: For so the Lord has commanded us: 'I have placed you as a light for the Gentiles, so that you may be for salvation to the end of the earth.'"
verses.13:48: When the Gentiles heard this, they began rejoicing and glorifying the word of the Lord, and as many as had been appointed to eternal life believed.
verses.13:49: And the word of the Lord was spreading throughout the entire region.
verses.13:50: But the Jews incited the devout women of high standing and the leading men of the city, and stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and drove them out of their territory.
verses.13:51: But they shook off the dust of their feet against them and went to Iconium.
verses.13:52: And the disciples were being filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
verses.14:1: Now it happened in Iconium that they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews and spoke in such a way that a great multitude of both Jews and Greeks believed.
verses.14:2: But the Jews who disbelieved stirred up and embittered the souls of the Gentiles against the brothers.
verses.14:3: Therefore they stayed for a considerable time, speaking boldly in the Lord, who was bearing witness to the word of His grace, granting signs and wonders to take place through their hands.
verses.14:4: But the multitude of the city was divided, and some were with the Jews, while others were with the apostles.
verses.14:5: And when a move was made by both the Gentiles and the Jews, along with their rulers, to mistreat and stone them,
verses.14:6: becoming aware of it, they fled to the cities of Lycaonia—Lystra and Derbe—and to the surrounding region,
verses.14:7: and there they continued proclaiming the good news.
verses.14:8: Now in Lystra a certain man without strength in his feet was sitting, lame from his mother's womb, who had never walked.
verses.14:9: This man heard Paul speaking; and Paul, fixing his gaze on him and seeing that he had faith to be made well,
verses.14:10: said with a loud voice, "Stand upright on your feet!" And he leaped up and began walking.
verses.14:11: When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voice in Lycaonian, saying, "The gods, having become like men, have come down to us!"
verses.14:12: And they began calling Barnabas Zeus, and Paul Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.
verses.14:13: And the priest of Zeus, whose temple was in front of the city, brought bulls and garlands to the gates and wanted to offer sacrifice together with the crowds.
verses.14:14: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard of this, they tore their garments and rushed out into the crowd, crying out
verses.14:15: and saying, "Men, why are you doing these things? We too are men of the same nature as you, proclaiming the good news to you to turn from these worthless things to a living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all that is in them.
verses.14:16: In the generations gone by, He permitted all the nations to walk in their own ways;
verses.14:17: yet He did not leave Himself without witness, doing good by giving you rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness."
verses.14:18: Even by saying these things, they barely restrained the crowds from offering sacrifice to them.
verses.14:19: But Jews came from Antioch and Iconium, and after persuading the crowds, they stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, supposing him to be dead.
verses.14:20: But while the disciples stood around him, he got up and entered the city. And the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.
verses.14:21: After proclaiming the good news to that city and making many disciples, they returned to Lystra and to Iconium and to Antioch,
verses.14:22: strengthening the souls of the disciples, encouraging them to continue in the faith, and saying that through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of God.
verses.14:23: When they had appointed elders for them in every church, having prayed with fasting, they committed them to the Lord in whom they had believed.
verses.14:24: Then, passing through Pisidia, they came into Pamphylia,
verses.14:25: and after speaking the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
verses.14:26: From there they sailed away to Antioch, from which they had been commended to the grace of God for the work that they had completed.
verses.14:27: When they arrived and gathered the church together, they reported all that God had done with them, and how He had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.
verses.14:28: And they stayed no little time with the disciples.
verses.15:1: Now some men came down from Judea and were teaching the brothers, "Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved."
verses.15:2: When Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and debate with them, they appointed Paul and Barnabas and some others among them to go up to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem concerning this question.
verses.15:3: So, having been sent on their way by the church, they passed through both Phoenicia and Samaria, recounting in detail the conversion of the Gentiles, and they brought great joy to all the brothers.
verses.15:4: When they arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church and the apostles and the elders, and they reported all that God had done with them.
verses.15:5: But some of those from the sect of the Pharisees who had believed stood up, saying, "It is necessary to circumcise them and to command them to keep the law of Moses."
verses.15:6: Then the apostles and the elders gathered together to look into this matter.
verses.15:7: After there had been much debate, Peter stood up and said to them, "Brothers, you know that in the early days God made a choice among you, that by my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the gospel and believe.
verses.15:8: And God, who knows the heart, bore witness to them by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as He also did to us;
verses.15:9: and He made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.
verses.15:10: Now therefore, why are you putting God to the test by placing a yoke on the neck of the disciples that neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
verses.15:11: On the contrary, we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus we are saved, in the same way as they also are."
verses.15:12: Then all the multitude fell silent, and they listened to Barnabas and Paul as they recounted all the signs and wonders that God had done among the Gentiles through them.
verses.15:13: After they became silent, James responded, saying, "Brothers, listen to me.
verses.15:14: Simeon has related how God first showed His care to take from the Gentiles a people for His name.
verses.15:15: And with this the words of the prophets agree, just as it is written:
verses.15:16: 'After these things I will return, and I will rebuild the fallen tabernacle of David; I will rebuild its ruins, and I will restore it,
verses.15:17: so that the rest of mankind may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles upon whom My name has been called, says the Lord, who makes these things
verses.15:19: Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those from the Gentiles who are turning to God,
verses.15:20: but rather write to them to abstain from the pollutions of idols, and from sexual immorality, and from what is strangled, and from blood.
verses.15:21: For from ancient generations Moses has had in every city those who proclaim him, since he is read in the synagogues every Sabbath."
verses.15:22: Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, together with the whole church, to choose men from among themselves to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas—Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, leading men among the brothers—
verses.15:23: writing by their hand: "The apostles and the elders, brothers, to the brothers from the Gentiles throughout Antioch and Syria and Cilicia: Greetings.
verses.15:24: Since we have heard that some who went out from us have troubled you with words, unsettling your souls, though we gave them no instruction,
verses.15:25: it seemed good to us, having come to one accord, to choose men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
verses.15:26: men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.15:27: Therefore we have sent Judas and Silas, who will themselves also report the same things by word of mouth.
verses.15:28: For it has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things:
verses.15:29: that you abstain from things sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves free from these, you will do well. Farewell."
verses.15:30: So when they were sent off, they went down to Antioch, and having gathered the multitude together, they delivered the letter.
verses.15:31: When they read it, they rejoiced over the encouragement.
verses.15:32: And Judas and Silas, who were prophets themselves as well, encouraged the brothers with many words and strengthened them.
verses.15:33: After spending some time there, they were sent off in peace by the brothers to those who had sent them.
verses.15:35: But Paul and Barnabas remained in Antioch, teaching and proclaiming the good news of the word of the Lord, along with many others as well.
verses.15:36: Now after some days Paul said to Barnabas, "Let us return and visit the brothers in every city in which we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing."
verses.15:37: Now Barnabas wanted to take along John, called Mark, as well.
verses.15:38: But Paul thought it best not to take along this man who had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia and had not gone with them to the work.
verses.15:39: And there arose such a sharp disagreement that they separated from one another, and Barnabas took Mark with him and sailed away to Cyprus,
verses.15:40: while Paul chose Silas and departed, having been commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.
verses.15:41: And he went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
verses.16:1: And he arrived also at Derbe and at Lystra. And look, a certain disciple was there by the name of Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman, though his father was a Greek,
verses.16:2: who was well spoken of by the brothers in Lystra and Iconium.
verses.16:3: Paul wanted this man to go out with him, and taking him, he circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those places, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
verses.16:4: Now as they were traveling through the cities, they were delivering to them the decrees to keep that had been decided by the apostles and elders who were in Jerusalem.
verses.16:5: So then the churches were being established firmly in the faith and were increasing in number day by day.
verses.16:6: And they passed through the Phrygian and Galatian region, having been prevented by the Holy Spirit from speaking the word in Asia.
verses.16:7: And having come up to Mysia, they were trying to go into Bithynia, and the Spirit of Jesus did not permit them.
verses.16:8: So passing by Mysia, they went down to Troas.
verses.16:9: And a vision appeared to Paul during the night: a certain Macedonian man was standing and appealing to him and saying, "Cross over into Macedonia and help us."
verses.16:10: Now when he saw the vision, we immediately sought to depart for Macedonia, concluding that God had summoned us to proclaim the gospel to them.
verses.16:11: Therefore, setting sail from Troas, we ran a straight course to Samothrace, and on the next day to Neapolis,
verses.16:12: and from there to Philippi, which is a leading city of the district of Macedonia, a colony. And we were staying in this city for some days.
verses.16:13: And on the Sabbath day we went outside the gate beside a river, where we supposed there was a place of prayer; and sitting down, we were speaking to the women who had come together.
verses.16:14: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple from the city of Thyatira, a worshiper of God, was listening, whose heart the Lord opened to pay attention to what was being spoken by Paul.
verses.16:15: Now when she and her household were baptized, she appealed, saying, "If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house and stay." And she prevailed upon us.
verses.16:16: Now it happened as we were going to the place of prayer that a certain slave girl having a spirit of divination met us, who was bringing much profit to her masters by fortune-telling.
verses.16:17: Following after Paul and us, she kept crying out, saying, "These men are slaves of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you a way of salvation."
