verses.16:18: And she kept doing this for many days. But Paul, becoming greatly annoyed, turned and said to the spirit, "I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her." And it came out at that very hour.
verses.16:19: But when her masters saw that their hope of profit had gone out, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers.
verses.16:20: And having brought them to the chief magistrates, they said, "These men, being Jews, are throwing our city into turmoil,
verses.16:21: and are proclaiming customs that are not lawful for us to accept or to practice, being Romans."
verses.16:22: And the crowd rose up together against them, and the chief magistrates tore off their garments and gave orders to beat them with rods.
verses.16:23: And after inflicting many blows upon them, they threw them into prison, commanding the jailer to guard them securely.
verses.16:24: Having received such a command, he threw them into the inner prison and secured their feet in the stocks.
verses.16:25: Now about midnight, Paul and Silas, praying, were singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening intently to them.
verses.16:26: And suddenly a great earthquake occurred, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened, and everyone's bonds were unfastened.
verses.16:27: Now when the jailer woke up and saw the prison doors opened, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, supposing that the prisoners had escaped.
verses.16:28: But Paul called out with a loud voice, saying, "Do no harm to yourself, for we are all here."
verses.16:29: And asking for lights, he rushed in and, trembling, fell down before Paul and Silas.
verses.16:30: And bringing them outside, he said, "Sirs, what must I do in order to be saved?"
verses.16:31: And they said, "Believe on the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household."
verses.16:32: And they spoke the word of the Lord to him along with all who were in his house.
verses.16:33: And taking them at that hour of the night, he washed their wounds, and immediately he and all who were his were baptized.
verses.16:34: And bringing them up into the house, he set a table before them and rejoiced greatly with his whole household, having believed in God.
verses.16:35: Now when day came, the chief magistrates sent the officers, saying, "Release those men."
verses.16:36: And the jailer reported these words to Paul: "The chief magistrates have sent word that you may be released. Now therefore, come out and go in peace."
verses.16:37: But Paul said to them, "Having beaten us publicly without a trial, men who are Romans, they threw us into prison; and now are they thrusting us out secretly? No indeed! Rather, let them come themselves and bring us out."
verses.16:38: And the officers reported these words to the chief magistrates; and they became afraid upon hearing that they were Romans.
verses.16:39: And they came and appealed to them, and after bringing them out, they kept asking them to depart from the city.
verses.16:40: And having come out of the prison, they went to Lydia's house; and when they saw the brothers, they encouraged them and departed.
verses.17:1: Now when they had traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.
verses.17:2: And according to Paul's custom, he went in to them, and for three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
verses.17:3: explaining and demonstrating that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead, and saying, "This is the Christ, Jesus, whom I am proclaiming to you."
verses.17:4: And some of them were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a large multitude of the devout Greeks and not a few of the leading women.
verses.17:5: But the Jews, becoming jealous and taking along some wicked men from the marketplace, formed a mob and threw the city into an uproar; and descending upon the house of Jason, they were seeking to bring them out to the public assembly.
verses.17:6: And when they did not find them, they dragged Jason and some brothers before the city officials, shouting, "These men who have thrown the inhabited world into turmoil have come here as well,
verses.17:7: whom Jason has welcomed; and they all act contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus."
verses.17:8: And they agitated the crowd and the city officials who heard these things,
verses.17:9: and after taking security from Jason and the rest, they released them.
verses.17:10: Now the brothers immediately sent both Paul and Silas away by night to Berea, and when they arrived, they went into the synagogue of the Jews.
verses.17:11: Now these were more noble-minded than those in Thessalonica; they received the word with all eagerness, examining the Scriptures daily to see whether these things were so.
verses.17:12: Therefore many of them believed, along with not a few Greek women of high standing and men.
verses.17:13: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that the word of God had been proclaimed by Paul in Berea also, they came there as well, stirring up and agitating the crowds.
verses.17:14: Then immediately the brothers sent Paul away to go as far as the sea, while both Silas and Timothy remained there.
verses.17:15: Now those who escorted Paul brought him as far as Athens; and after receiving a command for Silas and Timothy to come to him as quickly as possible, they departed.
verses.17:16: Now while Paul was waiting for them in Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he observed that the city was full of idols.
verses.17:17: So he was reasoning in the synagogue with the Jews and the devout worshipers, and in the marketplace every day with those who happened to be there.
verses.17:18: And some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also were debating with him. Some were saying, "What would this babbler wish to say?" Others said, "He seems to be a proclaimer of foreign deities," because he was preaching the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.
verses.17:19: And taking hold of him, they brought him to the Areopagus, saying, "May we know what this new teaching is that is being spoken by you?
verses.17:20: For you are bringing some strange things to our ears; therefore we wish to know what these things mean."
verses.17:21: Now all the Athenians and the foreigners residing there spent their time in nothing other than telling or hearing something new.
verses.17:22: Then Paul stood in the midst of the Areopagus and said, "Men of Athens, I observe that in every respect you are very religious;
verses.17:23: for while passing through and closely observing your objects of worship, I also found an altar on which had been inscribed, 'To an unknown god.' What therefore you worship in ignorance, this I proclaim to you.
verses.17:24: The God who made the world and everything in it, since He is Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands,
verses.17:25: nor is He served by human hands, as though He needed anything, since He Himself gives to all life and breath and all things.
verses.17:26: And He made from one every nation of mankind to live on the entire face of the earth, having determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their habitation,
verses.17:27: so that they would seek God, if perhaps they might grope for Him and find Him, though indeed He is not far from each one of us;
verses.17:28: for in Him we live and move and exist, as even some of your own poets have said, 'For we are also His offspring.'
verses.17:29: Being therefore the offspring of God, we ought not to suppose that the Divine Nature is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by the craft and imagination of man.
verses.17:30: Therefore, having overlooked the times of ignorance, God now declares to people that all everywhere should repent,
verses.17:31: because He has fixed a day on which He will judge the inhabited world in righteousness through a man whom He has appointed, having provided assurance to all by raising Him from the dead."
verses.17:32: Now when they heard of a resurrection of the dead, some began mocking, while others said, "We will hear you concerning this again."
verses.17:33: So Paul went out from their midst.
verses.17:34: But some men joined him and believed, among whom were also Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
verses.18:1: After these things he departed from Athens and came to Corinth.
verses.18:2: And finding a certain Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to depart from Rome, he went to them,
verses.18:3: and because he was of the same trade, he stayed with them and they worked together, for by trade they were tentmakers.
verses.18:4: And he was reasoning in the synagogue every Sabbath, and persuading Jews and Greeks.
verses.18:5: Now when both Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul became wholly occupied with the word, solemnly testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
verses.18:6: But when they opposed him and blasphemed, he shook out his garments and said to them, "Your blood be on your own head! I am clean; from now on I will go to the Gentiles."
verses.18:7: And leaving from there, he went into the house of a man named Titius Justus, a worshiper of God, whose house was adjacent to the synagogue.
verses.18:8: Now Crispus, the synagogue ruler, believed in the Lord together with his whole household; and many of the Corinthians, as they heard, were believing and being baptized.
verses.18:9: And the Lord said to Paul in the night by a vision, "Do not be afraid, but speak and do not keep silent,
verses.18:10: because I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, because I have many people in this city."
verses.18:11: And he settled there for a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
verses.18:12: Now while Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews rose up with one accord against Paul and brought him before the tribunal,
verses.18:13: saying, "This man is persuading people to worship God contrary to the law."
verses.18:14: But just as Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, "If it were a matter of some wrongdoing or wicked crime, O Jews, I would reasonably bear with you;
verses.18:15: but if there are questions about words and names and your own law, see to it yourselves; I do not wish to be a judge of these things."
verses.18:16: And he drove them away from the tribunal.
verses.18:17: Then they all took hold of Sosthenes, the synagogue ruler, and began beating him in front of the tribunal; and Gallio was not concerned about any of these things.
verses.18:18: Now Paul, having remained many days longer, took leave of the brothers and set sail for Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila, having cut his hair in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.
verses.18:19: And they arrived at Ephesus, and he left them there; but he himself entered the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.
verses.18:20: And when they asked him to stay for a longer time, he did not consent,
verses.18:21: but taking leave of them and saying, "I will return to you again, if God wills," he set sail from Ephesus.
verses.18:22: And when he had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church, and then went down to Antioch.
verses.18:23: And after spending some time there, he departed, passing successively through the Galatian region and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
verses.18:24: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, an eloquent man, arrived at Ephesus; he was mighty in the Scriptures.
verses.18:25: This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in spirit, he was speaking and teaching accurately the things concerning Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.
verses.18:26: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained the way of God to him more accurately.
verses.18:27: And when he wished to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples to welcome him; and when he arrived, he greatly helped those who had believed through grace,
verses.18:28: for he vigorously refuted the Jews in public, demonstrating through the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
verses.19:1: Now it happened that while Apollos was in Corinth, Paul, having passed through the upper regions, came to Ephesus and found some disciples.
verses.19:2: And he said to them, "Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?" And they said to him, "No, we have not even heard whether there is a Holy Spirit."
verses.19:3: And he said, "Into what then were you baptized?" And they said, "Into John's baptism."
verses.19:4: And Paul said, "John baptized with a baptism of repentance, telling the people that they should believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Jesus."
verses.19:5: And when they heard this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.19:6: And when Paul had laid hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they were speaking in tongues and prophesying.
verses.19:7: And there were in all about twelve men.
verses.19:8: And having entered the synagogue, he spoke boldly for three months, reasoning and persuading concerning the kingdom of God.
verses.19:9: But when some were becoming hardened and disobedient, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he withdrew from them and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
verses.19:10: And this went on for two years, so that all who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks.
verses.19:11: And God was performing extraordinary miracles through the hands of Paul,
verses.19:12: so that handkerchiefs or aprons were even carried from his skin to those who were sick, and the diseases left them, and the evil spirits went out.
verses.19:13: Now some of the traveling Jewish exorcists also attempted to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those who had the evil spirits, saying, "I adjure you by Jesus whom Paul proclaims."
verses.19:14: And seven sons of a certain Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.
verses.19:15: And the evil spirit answered and said to them, "Jesus I recognize, and Paul I know about, but who are you?"
verses.19:16: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped upon them, subdued all of them, and overpowered them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
verses.19:17: And this became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who lived in Ephesus; and fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was being magnified.
verses.19:18: And many of those who had believed kept coming, confessing and disclosing their practices.
verses.19:19: And a considerable number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books together and were burning them before everyone; and they calculated their value and found it to be fifty thousand pieces of silver.
verses.19:20: In this way the word of the Lord was growing mightily and prevailing.
verses.19:21: Now when these things had been accomplished, Paul resolved in the spirit to travel to Jerusalem after passing through Macedonia and Achaia, saying, "After I have been there, I must also see Rome."
verses.19:22: And having sent into Macedonia two of those who assisted him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a time.
verses.19:23: Now about that time there arose no small disturbance concerning the Way.
verses.19:24: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, who made silver shrines of Artemis, was bringing no small business to the craftsmen.
verses.19:25: Having gathered these together, along with the workers in similar trades, he said, "Men, you know that our prosperity is from this business,
verses.19:26: and you see and hear that not only in Ephesus, but in almost all of Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away a considerable crowd, saying that those made with hands are not gods.
verses.19:27: And not only is there danger that this trade of ours will fall into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be counted as nothing, and that she is even about to be brought down from her majesty, she whom all Asia and the inhabited world worship."
verses.19:28: And when they heard this and became full of rage, they were crying out, saying, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"
verses.19:29: And the city was filled with the confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, Paul's traveling companions.
verses.19:30: And when Paul wanted to go in among the people, the disciples would not permit him.
verses.19:31: And some of the Asiarchs as well, who were friends of his, sent to him and urged him not to venture into the theater.
verses.19:32: So then, some were shouting one thing and some another, for the assembly was in confusion, and the majority did not know for what reason they had come together.
verses.19:33: And some from the crowd prompted Alexander, since the Jews had put him forward; and Alexander, motioning with his hand, wanted to make a defense to the people.
verses.19:34: But when they recognized that he was a Jew, a single cry arose from them all as they shouted for about two hours, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"
verses.19:35: And after quieting the crowd, the town clerk said, "Men of Ephesus, what person is there who does not know that the city of the Ephesians is temple keeper of the great Artemis and of that which fell from heaven?
verses.19:36: Therefore, since these things are undeniable, you ought to remain quiet and to do nothing rash.
verses.19:37: For you have brought these men, who are neither temple robbers nor blasphemers of our goddess.
verses.19:38: So then, if Demetrius and the craftsmen who are with him have a complaint against anyone, the courts are in session and there are proconsuls; let them bring charges against one another.
verses.19:39: But if you are seeking anything concerning other matters, it will be settled in the lawful assembly.
verses.19:40: For indeed we are in danger of being charged with rioting concerning today, since there is no cause, and in regard to it we will not be able to give an account for this disorderly gathering." And having said these things, he dismissed the assembly.
verses.20:1: Now after the uproar ceased, Paul sent for the disciples and encouraged them, and after saying farewell, he departed to travel to Macedonia.
verses.20:2: After passing through those regions and encouraging them with many words, he came to Greece,
verses.20:3: and spent three months there. When a plot was made against him by the Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he decided to return through Macedonia.
verses.20:4: Now accompanying him were Sopater son of Pyrrhus, of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
verses.20:5: These men came and were waiting for us in Troas.
verses.20:6: But we sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas within five days, where we stayed seven days.
verses.20:7: Now on the first day of the week, when we were gathered together to break bread, Paul was speaking to them, intending to leave the next day, and he prolonged his speech until midnight.
verses.20:8: Now there were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered together.
verses.20:9: A certain young man named Eutychus, sitting on the windowsill, was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul kept speaking longer and longer; and overcome by sleep, he fell down from the third story and was picked up dead.
verses.20:10: But Paul went down and fell upon him, and embracing him, he said, "Do not be alarmed, for his life is in him."
verses.20:11: Then he went back up, broke the bread and ate, and after conversing for a long while until daybreak, he departed.
verses.20:12: And they took the boy away alive and were comforted beyond measure.
verses.20:13: But we went ahead to the ship and set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul on board from there; for he had arranged it this way, intending himself to go on foot.
verses.20:14: When he met us at Assos, we took him on board and came to Mitylene.
verses.20:15: Sailing away from there, on the following day we arrived opposite Chios; the next day we crossed over to Samos; and on the day after that we came to Miletus.
verses.20:16: For Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus, so that he would not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hurrying, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
verses.20:17: Now from Miletus he sent to Ephesus and summoned the elders of the church.
verses.20:18: When they came to him, he said to them, "You yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, how I conducted myself with you the whole time,
verses.20:19: serving the Lord with all humility and with tears and trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews;
verses.20:20: how I did not hold back from declaring to you anything that was beneficial and from teaching you publicly and from house to house,
verses.20:21: solemnly testifying to both Jews and Greeks of repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus.
verses.20:22: And now, look, bound in spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing the things that will happen to me there,
verses.20:23: except that the Holy Spirit solemnly testifies to me in every city, saying that chains and afflictions await me.
verses.20:24: Yet I hold my life to be of no account, nor dear to myself, so that I may complete my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify solemnly to the gospel of the grace of God.
verses.20:25: And now, look, I know that none of you among whom I went about proclaiming the kingdom will see my face again.
verses.20:26: Therefore I testify to you this very day that I am innocent of the blood of all,
verses.20:27: for I did not hold back from declaring to you the entire purpose of God.
verses.20:28: Watch carefully over yourselves and all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has appointed you overseers, to shepherd the church of God, which He acquired through His own blood.
verses.20:29: I know that after my departure fierce wolves will come in among you, not sparing the flock;
verses.20:30: and from among your own selves men will rise up, speaking distorted things to draw away the disciples after themselves.
verses.20:31: Therefore be watchful, remembering that for three years, night and day, I did not cease admonishing each one with tears.
verses.20:32: And now I entrust you to God and to the word of His grace, which is able to build you up and to give the inheritance among all those who have been sanctified.
verses.20:33: I have coveted no one's silver or gold or clothing.
verses.20:34: You yourselves know that these hands provided for my needs and for those who were with me.
verses.20:35: In everything I demonstrated to you that by laboring in this manner we must support the weak, and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that He Himself said, 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'"
verses.20:36: When he had said these things, he knelt down and prayed with all of them.
verses.20:37: There was much weeping among them all, and falling upon Paul's neck, they kissed him repeatedly,
verses.20:38: grieving most of all over the word he had spoken, that they would not see his face again. And they accompanied him to the ship.
verses.21:1: Now when we had torn ourselves away from them and set sail, running a straight course we came to Cos, and on the following day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
verses.21:2: And finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.
verses.21:3: And having sighted Cyprus and left it on the left, we kept sailing to Syria and landed at Tyre, for there the ship was to unload its cargo.
verses.21:4: And having sought out the disciples, we stayed there seven days; and they kept telling Paul through the Spirit not to set foot in Jerusalem.
verses.21:5: And when we had completed those days, we departed and went on our way, while all of them, with wives and children, escorted us until we were outside the city; and kneeling down on the beach and praying,
verses.21:6: we said farewell to one another and boarded the ship, while they returned to their own homes.
verses.21:7: When we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais, and having greeted the brothers, we stayed with them for one day.
verses.21:8: And on the next day we departed and came to Caesarea, and entering the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, we stayed with him.
verses.21:9: Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.
verses.21:10: While we were staying there for several days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
verses.21:11: And coming to us and taking Paul's belt, he bound his own feet and hands and said, "This is what the Holy Spirit says: 'In this way the Jews in Jerusalem will bind the man whose belt this is, and will hand him over into the hands of the Gentiles.'"
verses.21:12: Now when we heard these things, both we and the local residents began urging him not to go up to Jerusalem.
verses.21:13: Then Paul answered, "What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus."
verses.21:14: And since he would not be persuaded, we fell silent, saying, "Let the will of the Lord be done."
verses.21:15: Now after these days, having packed our belongings, we went up to Jerusalem.
verses.21:16: And some of the disciples from Caesarea also came with us, bringing us to a certain Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we were to lodge.
verses.21:17: And when we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us gladly.
verses.21:18: And on the following day Paul went in with us to James, and all the elders were present.
verses.21:19: And after greeting them, he related one by one the things that God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
verses.21:20: And when they heard this, they began glorifying God; and they said to him, "You see, brother, how many tens of thousands there are among the Jews of those who have believed, and they are all zealous for the law;
verses.21:21: and they have been informed about you that you teach all the Jews among the Gentiles apostasy from Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children nor to walk according to the customs.
verses.21:22: What then is to be done? They will certainly hear that you have come.
verses.21:23: Therefore do this that we tell you: we have four men who have a vow of their own.
verses.21:24: Take these men and purify yourself along with them, and pay the expenses for them so that they may shave their heads; and all will know that there is nothing to the things of which they have been informed about you, but that you yourself also walk properly, keeping the law.
verses.21:25: But concerning the Gentiles who have believed, we sent word, having decided that they should keep themselves from what is sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from what is strangled, and from sexual immorality."
verses.21:26: Then Paul took the men, and on the next day, having purified himself along with them, he went into the temple, giving notice of the completion of the days of purification, until the offering was presented for each one of them.
verses.21:27: Now when the seven days were about to be completed, the Jews from Asia, seeing him in the temple, stirred up the whole crowd and laid hands on him,
verses.21:28: crying out, "Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against the people and the law and this place; and furthermore, he has even brought Greeks into the temple and has defiled this holy place."
verses.21:29: For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him, and they supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.
verses.21:30: And the whole city was thrown into commotion, and the people ran together; and seizing Paul, they dragged him out of the temple, and immediately the doors were shut.
verses.21:31: And while they were seeking to kill him, a report went up to the commander of the cohort that all Jerusalem was in confusion.
verses.21:32: At once he took soldiers and centurions and ran down to them; and when they saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
verses.21:33: Then the commander came up, took hold of him, and ordered him to be bound with two chains; and he began inquiring who he was and what he had done.
verses.21:34: But some in the crowd were shouting one thing and some another; and since he could not ascertain the facts because of the uproar, he ordered him to be brought into the barracks.
verses.21:35: And when he came to the steps, it happened that he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd,
verses.21:36: for the multitude of the people kept following, crying out, "Away with him!"
verses.21:37: And as Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he said to the commander, "May I say something to you?" And he said, "Do you know Greek?
verses.21:38: Then you are not the Egyptian who before these days stirred up a revolt and led the four thousand men of the Assassins out into the wilderness?"
verses.21:39: But Paul said, "I am a Jewish man, from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city; and I beg you, permit me to speak to the people."
verses.21:40: And when he had given him permission, Paul, standing on the steps, motioned with his hand to the people; and when a great silence had fallen, he addressed them in the Hebrew dialect, saying:
verses.22:1: "Men, brothers and fathers, listen to my defense to you now."
verses.22:2: And when they heard that he was addressing them in the Hebrew dialect, they became even quieter. And he said:
verses.22:3: "I am a Jewish man, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, educated according to the strictness of the ancestral law, being zealous for God just as all of you are today,
verses.22:4: who persecuted this Way to the death, binding and handing over into prisons both men and women,
verses.22:5: as also the high priest testifies for me, along with all the council of elders. From them I also received letters to the brothers and was going to Damascus to bring even those who were there bound to Jerusalem, so that they might be punished.
verses.22:6: Now it happened that as I was going along and drawing near to Damascus, about noon, suddenly a great light from heaven flashed around me,
verses.22:7: and I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?'
verses.22:8: And I answered, 'Who are You, Lord?' And He said to me, 'I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you are persecuting.'
verses.22:9: Now those who were with me saw the light, yet they did not hear the voice of the One speaking to me.
verses.22:10: And I said, 'What shall I do, Lord?' And the Lord said to me, 'Get up and go into Damascus, and there you will be told about all the things that have been appointed for you to do.'
verses.22:11: And since I could not see because of the glory of that light, being led by the hand by those who were with me, I came into Damascus.
verses.22:12: Now a certain Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well spoken of by all the Jews who lived there,
verses.22:13: came to me, and standing beside me, said to me, 'Brother Saul, receive your sight!' And in that very hour I looked up at him.
verses.22:14: And he said, 'The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from His mouth,
verses.22:15: for you will be a witness for Him to all people of what you have seen and heard.
verses.22:16: And now why do you delay? Get up, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on His name.'
verses.22:17: Now it happened that when I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, I fell into a trance
verses.22:18: and saw Him saying to me, 'Hurry and get out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not accept your testimony about Me.'
verses.22:19: And I said, 'Lord, they themselves know that throughout the synagogues I was imprisoning and beating those who believed in You;
verses.22:20: and when the blood of Your witness Stephen was being shed, I myself was also standing by and approving, and guarding the garments of those who were killing him.'
verses.22:21: And He said to me, 'Go, for I will send you far away to the Gentiles.'"
verses.22:22: Now they listened to him up to this word, and then they raised their voices, saying, "Away with such a man from the earth, for he ought not to live!"
verses.22:23: And as they were shouting and throwing off their garments and tossing dust into the air,
verses.22:24: the commander ordered him to be brought into the barracks, saying that he should be examined by scourging, so that he might find out for what reason they were shouting against him like this.
verses.22:25: But when they had stretched him out with the leather straps, Paul said to the centurion who was standing by, "Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman and uncondemned?"
verses.22:26: And when the centurion heard this, he went to the commander and reported it, saying, "What are you about to do? For this man is a Roman."
verses.22:27: So the commander came and said to him, "Tell me, are you a Roman?" And he said, "Yes."
verses.22:28: And the commander answered, "I acquired this citizenship for a large sum." And Paul said, "But I was even born a citizen."
verses.22:29: Immediately, therefore, those who were about to examine him withdrew from him; and the commander also was afraid when he realized that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
verses.22:30: Now on the next day, wishing to ascertain the facts as to why he was being accused by the Jews, he unbound him and ordered the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin to assemble; and bringing Paul down, he set him before them.
verses.23:1: Looking intently at the Sanhedrin, Paul said, "Men, brothers, I have conducted my life before God in all good conscience until this day."
verses.23:2: And the high priest Ananias ordered those standing beside him to strike his mouth.
verses.23:3: Then Paul said to him, "God is going to strike you, whitewashed wall! And do you sit judging me according to the law, and yet violating the law command me to be struck?"
verses.23:4: And those standing by said, "Do you revile God's high priest?"
verses.23:5: And Paul said, "I did not know, brothers, that he is high priest; for it is written, 'You must not speak evil of a ruler of your people.'"
verses.23:6: Now knowing that one part was Sadducees and the other Pharisees, Paul cried out in the Sanhedrin, "Men, brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees! Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am on trial."
verses.23:7: And as he was saying this, a dissension arose between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.
verses.23:8: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit, but the Pharisees acknowledge both.
verses.23:9: And a loud clamor arose, and some of the scribes of the party of the Pharisees stood up and were arguing sharply, saying, "We find nothing wrong in this man; and what if a spirit spoke to him, or an angel—"
verses.23:10: And as a great dissension developed, the commander, fearing that Paul might be torn to pieces by them, commanded the troops to go down and seize him from their midst and bring him into the barracks.
verses.23:11: On the following night the Lord stood beside him and said, "Take courage, for as you have testified to the things concerning Me in Jerusalem, so you must also testify in Rome."
verses.23:12: When day came, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they killed Paul.
verses.23:13: Now there were more than forty who made this sworn conspiracy.
verses.23:14: They came to the chief priests and the elders and said, "We have solemnly bound ourselves under a curse to taste nothing until we kill Paul.
verses.23:15: Now therefore, you, along with the Sanhedrin, notify the commander so that he will bring him down to you, as though you were about to investigate the matters concerning him more closely; and as for us, before he comes near, we are ready to kill him."
verses.23:16: But the son of Paul's sister heard about the ambush, and he came and entered the barracks and reported it to Paul.
verses.23:17: Then Paul called one of the centurions to him and said, "Lead this young man to the commander, for he has something to report to him."
verses.23:18: So he took him and brought him to the commander and said, "The prisoner Paul called me to him and asked me to bring this young man to you, since he has something to tell you."
verses.23:19: And the commander took him by the hand and, withdrawing privately, began to inquire, "What is it that you have to report to me?"
verses.23:20: And he said, "The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the Sanhedrin tomorrow, as though you were going to inquire somewhat more closely concerning him.
verses.23:21: Therefore do not be persuaded by them, for more than forty men from among them are lying in ambush for him, who have bound themselves under a curse neither to eat nor to drink until they kill him; and now they are ready, waiting for the promise from you."
verses.23:22: So the commander dismissed the young man, charging him, "Tell no one that you have reported these things to me."
verses.23:23: And calling two of the centurions to him, he said, "Make ready two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, and seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen, at the third hour of the night."
verses.23:24: They were also to provide mounts so that, having mounted Paul, they might bring him safely to Felix the governor.
verses.23:25: And he wrote a letter having this form:
verses.23:26: "Claudius Lysias, to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.
verses.23:27: This man was seized by the Jews and was about to be killed by them, when I came upon them with the troops and rescued him, having learned that he is a Roman.
verses.23:28: And wanting to ascertain the charge for which they were accusing him, I brought him down to their Sanhedrin.
verses.23:29: I found him to be accused concerning questions of their law, yet having no accusation deserving death or chains.
verses.23:30: When it was disclosed to me that there would be a plot against the man, I sent him to you at once, also instructing the accusers to speak against him before you."
verses.23:31: So the soldiers, in accordance with what had been ordered them, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
verses.23:32: And on the next day, leaving the horsemen to go on with him, they returned to the barracks.
verses.23:33: When these entered Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.
verses.23:34: When he had read it and asked from what province he was, and learned that he was from Cilicia,
verses.23:35: "I will give you a full hearing," he said, "when your accusers arrive as well," and he ordered him to be kept under guard in Herod's praetorium.
verses.24:1: Now after five days the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a certain orator named Tertullus, and they presented their case to the governor against Paul.
verses.24:2: And when he had been summoned, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, "Since we enjoy great peace through you, and since reforms are taking place for this nation through your foresight,
verses.24:3: in every way and in every place we acknowledge this, most excellent Felix, with all gratitude.
verses.24:4: But so that I may not detain you any further, I beg you in your kindness to hear us briefly.
verses.24:5: For we have found this man to be a pest and one who stirs up dissensions among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,
verses.24:6: who even attempted to profane the temple, and we seized him.
verses.24:8: By examining him yourself, you will be able to learn from him concerning all these things of which we accuse him."
verses.24:9: And the Jews also joined in the charge, asserting that these things were so.
verses.24:10: When the governor nodded to him to speak, Paul answered, "Knowing that for many years you have been a judge to this nation, I gladly make my defense concerning myself,
verses.24:11: since you are able to verify that it has been no more than twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem to worship;
verses.24:12: and they did not find me disputing with anyone or stirring up a crowd either in the temple or in the synagogues or throughout the city,
verses.24:13: nor can they prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.
verses.24:14: But this I confess to you, that according to the Way, which they call a sect, I worship the God of our fathers, believing everything in accordance with the law and written in the prophets,
verses.24:15: having a hope in God, which these men themselves also accept, that there is going to be a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.
verses.24:16: Because of this, I myself also take pains to have a blameless conscience toward God and toward people at all times.
verses.24:17: Now after several years I came to bring alms to my nation and to present offerings,
verses.24:18: in the course of which they found me purified in the temple, with neither crowd nor uproar.
verses.24:19: But some Jews from Asia—they ought to be present before you and bring charges if they have anything against me.
verses.24:20: Or let these men themselves say what wrongdoing they found when I stood before the Sanhedrin,
verses.24:21: other than this one statement that I cried out while standing among them, 'Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am on trial before you today.'"
verses.24:22: Then Felix, having quite accurate knowledge of the matters concerning the Way, put them off, saying, "When Lysias the commander comes down, I will decide your case."
verses.24:23: He gave orders to the centurion for him to be kept under guard, yet to have some freedom, and not to prevent any of his own people from serving him.
verses.24:24: Now after some days, Felix arrived with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, and he sent for Paul and heard him concerning faith in Christ Jesus.
verses.24:25: And as he was reasoning about righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix became frightened and answered, "Go away for the present, and when I find an opportunity I will summon you."
verses.24:26: At the same time he was also hoping that money would be given to him by Paul; therefore he also sent for him rather frequently and conversed with him.
verses.24:27: When two years had passed, Felix received Porcius Festus as his successor; and wanting to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul in chains.
verses.25:1: Festus then, having arrived in the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
verses.25:2: And the chief priests and the leading men of the Jews brought charges before him against Paul, and they were urging him,
verses.25:3: asking a favor against him that he would summon him to Jerusalem, while preparing an ambush to kill him along the way.
verses.25:4: Festus then answered that Paul was being kept in custody at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to depart shortly.
verses.25:5: "Therefore," he said, "let those among you who are in authority go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him."
verses.25:6: And after spending among them not more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea; and on the next day, sitting down on the judgment seat, he commanded Paul to be brought.
verses.25:7: And when he arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many and serious charges which they were not able to prove,
verses.25:8: while Paul spoke in his defense, "Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar have I committed any offense."
verses.25:9: But Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, answered Paul and said, "Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and there be tried before me concerning these things?"
verses.25:10: But Paul said, "I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where I ought to be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you also know very well.
verses.25:11: If, then, I am a wrongdoer and have committed anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die; but if there is nothing to the things of which these men accuse me, no one can hand me over to them as a favor. I appeal to Caesar."
verses.25:12: Then Festus, having conferred with the council, answered, "To Caesar you have appealed; to Caesar you will go."
verses.25:13: Now when several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.
verses.25:14: And while they were spending many days there, Festus laid the matters concerning Paul before the king, saying, "There is a certain man left behind as a prisoner by Felix,
verses.25:15: concerning whom, when I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews brought charges, asking for a sentence of condemnation against him.
verses.25:16: To them I answered that it is not the custom of the Romans to hand over any man as a favor before the accused has his accusers face to face and receives an opportunity for a defense concerning the charge.
verses.25:17: Therefore, when they had assembled here, making no delay, on the next day I sat down on the judgment seat and commanded the man to be brought.
verses.25:18: Concerning him, when the accusers stood up, they brought no charge of such evil things as I was supposing,
verses.25:19: but they had certain disputes against him concerning their own religion and concerning a certain Jesus, who had died, whom Paul kept asserting to be alive.
verses.25:20: And being at a loss as to the inquiry concerning these matters, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there be tried concerning these matters.
verses.25:21: But when Paul appealed to be kept in custody for the decision of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept until I could send him up to Caesar."
verses.25:22: And Agrippa said to Festus, "I myself would also like to hear the man." "Tomorrow," he said, "you will hear him."
verses.25:23: So on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the audience hall along with the military commanders and the prominent men of the city, at the command of Festus Paul was brought in.
verses.25:24: And Festus said, "King Agrippa, and all you men who are present here with us, you see this man, concerning whom the entire multitude of the Jews petitioned me both in Jerusalem and here, shouting that he ought not to live any longer.
verses.25:25: Yet I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death; and since he himself appealed to Augustus, I decided to send him.
verses.25:26: Concerning him I have nothing definite to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him out before you all, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after the examination has taken place, I may have something to write.
verses.25:27: For it seems unreasonable to me, in sending a prisoner, not also to indicate the charges against him."
verses.26:1: And Agrippa said to Paul, "You are permitted to speak for yourself." Then Paul stretched out his hand and began to make his defense:
verses.26:2: "Concerning all the things of which I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate that I am about to make my defense before you today,
verses.26:3: especially because you are an expert in all the customs and disputes among the Jews; therefore I beg you to listen to me patiently.
verses.26:4: My manner of life from youth, which from the beginning was spent among my own nation and in Jerusalem, all the Jews know,
verses.26:5: having known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived as a Pharisee.
verses.26:6: And now I stand on trial for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,
verses.26:7: to which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, O king.
verses.26:8: Why is it judged incredible among you if God raises the dead?
verses.26:9: I myself indeed thought that I ought to do many things in opposition to the name of Jesus the Nazarene.
verses.26:10: And this I also did in Jerusalem; and I myself locked up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests, and when they were being put to death, I cast my vote against them.
verses.26:11: And throughout all the synagogues, often punishing them, I kept trying to force them to blaspheme; and being furiously enraged against them, I kept pursuing them even to foreign cities.
verses.26:12: While thus engaged, as I was journeying to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests,
verses.26:13: at midday along the road I saw, O king, a light from heaven, brighter than the radiance of the sun, shining around me and those who were journeying with me.
verses.26:14: And when we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew dialect, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.'
verses.26:15: And I said, 'Who are You, Lord?' And the Lord said, 'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
verses.26:16: But rise and stand on your feet; for to this end I have appeared to you, to appoint you as a servant and a witness both of the things in which you have seen Me and of the things in which I will appear to you,
verses.26:17: delivering you from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I am sending you,
verses.26:18: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the authority of Satan to God, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those who have been sanctified by faith in Me.'
verses.26:19: Therefore, King Agrippa, I did not become disobedient to the heavenly vision,
verses.26:20: but kept declaring first to those in Damascus, and in Jerusalem, and throughout all the region of Judea, and to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, practicing deeds worthy of repentance.
verses.26:21: On account of these things, some Jews seized me in the temple and were trying to put me to death.
verses.26:22: Therefore, having obtained the help that comes from God, I stand to this day testifying to both small and great, saying nothing beyond what both the prophets and Moses said was going to take place:
verses.26:23: that the Christ must suffer, and that, as the first from the resurrection of the dead, He is going to proclaim light both to the people and to the Gentiles."
verses.26:24: And as he was saying these things in his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, "You are out of your mind, Paul! Your great learning is turning you to madness."
verses.26:25: But Paul said, "I am not out of my mind, most excellent Festus, but I am uttering words of truth and sober reason.
verses.26:26: For the king knows about these things, to whom I also speak boldly; for I am persuaded that none of these things has escaped his notice, because this has not been done in a corner.
verses.26:27: Do you believe the prophets, King Agrippa? I know that you believe."
verses.26:28: And Agrippa said to Paul, "In a short time you are trying to persuade me to act as a Christian."
verses.26:29: And Paul said, "I would pray to God that whether in a short time or in a long time, not only you, but also all who are listening to me today might become such as I also am, except for these chains."
verses.26:30: And the king stood up, and the governor and Bernice and those who were sitting with them,
verses.26:31: and when they had withdrawn, they were speaking to one another, saying, "This man is doing nothing worthy of death or chains."
verses.26:32: And Agrippa said to Festus, "This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar."
verses.27:1: Now when it was decided that we would sail for Italy, they handed over both Paul and some other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan cohort.
verses.27:2: Boarding a ship of Adramyttium that was about to sail to the places along Asia, we put out to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, being with us.
verses.27:3: The next day we put in at Sidon, and Julius, treating Paul kindly, permitted him to go to his friends to receive care.
verses.27:4: Putting out to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus because the winds were contrary.
verses.27:5: After sailing across the open sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came down to Myra in Lycia.
verses.27:6: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy, and he put us aboard it.
verses.27:7: Sailing slowly for many days and coming with difficulty off Cnidus, since the wind did not permit us to advance, we sailed under the lee of Crete off Salmone;
verses.27:8: and coasting along it with difficulty, we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near which was the city of Lasea.
verses.27:9: When considerable time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous because even the Fast had already gone by, Paul began to advise them,
verses.27:10: saying to them, "Men, I perceive that the voyage is going to be with damage and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives."
verses.27:11: But the centurion was persuaded more by the pilot and the shipowner than by what was being said by Paul.
verses.27:12: And because the harbor was unsuitable for wintering, the majority decided to put out to sea from there, if somehow they might reach Phoenix and winter there, a harbor of Crete facing southwest and northwest.
verses.27:13: When a gentle south wind began to blow, supposing that they had secured their purpose, they weighed anchor and began coasting close along Crete.
verses.27:14: Not long afterward, however, a tempestuous wind called Euraquilo struck down from it;
verses.27:15: and when the ship was caught and unable to face into the wind, we gave way and were driven along.
verses.27:16: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able with difficulty to gain control of the ship's boat.
verses.27:17: After hoisting it up, they used supports to undergird the ship; and fearing that they might be driven onto the Syrtis, they lowered the gear and so were driven along.
verses.27:18: Since we were being violently storm-tossed, on the next day they began to jettison the cargo,
verses.27:19: and on the third day they threw out the ship's tackle with their own hands.
verses.27:20: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no small storm was pressing upon us, from then on all hope of our being saved was stripped away.
verses.27:21: When they had gone a long time without food, Paul stood in the midst of them and said, "Men, you ought indeed to have listened to me and not put out to sea from Crete, and so spared yourselves this damage and loss.
verses.27:22: Yet now I advise you to take courage, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
verses.27:23: For this night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I also serve stood beside me,
verses.27:24: saying, 'Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar; and look, God has graciously granted to you all those who are sailing with you.'
verses.27:25: Therefore take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as it has been spoken to me.
verses.27:26: However, we must run aground on a certain island."
verses.27:27: Now when the fourteenth night came, as we were being driven about in the Adriatic Sea, around the middle of the night the sailors began to suspect that some land was drawing near to them.
verses.27:28: And taking soundings, they found twenty fathoms; and after moving a short distance farther and taking soundings again, they found fifteen fathoms.
verses.27:29: Fearing that we might run aground somewhere on rocky places, they cast four anchors from the stern and prayed for day to come.
verses.27:30: But as the sailors were seeking to escape from the ship and had lowered the ship's boat into the sea, under the pretext that they were about to lay out anchors from the bow,
verses.27:31: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, "Unless these men remain in the ship, you cannot be saved."
verses.27:32: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the ship's boat and let it fall away.
verses.27:33: Until day was about to come, Paul was urging everyone to take some food, saying, "Today is the fourteenth day that you have continued watching without food, having taken nothing.
verses.27:34: Therefore I urge you to take some food, for this is for your survival; for not a hair from the head of any one of you will perish."
verses.27:35: Having said these things, he took bread, gave thanks to God in the presence of all, broke it, and began to eat.
verses.27:36: All of them took courage and took some food themselves.
verses.27:37: Now in all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls in the ship.
verses.27:38: When they had eaten enough food, they began lightening the ship by throwing the wheat into the sea.
verses.27:39: When day came, they did not recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, onto which they planned to drive the ship ashore, if they could.
verses.27:40: And casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time loosening the lashings of the rudders; and hoisting the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.
verses.27:41: But striking a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground; and the bow stuck fast and remained immovable, while the stern was being broken up by the violence.
verses.27:42: Now the soldiers' plan was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim away and escape.
verses.27:43: But the centurion, wanting to bring Paul safely through, kept them from their purpose, and ordered those who were able to swim to throw themselves overboard first and get to land,
verses.27:44: and the rest, some on planks and others on various things from the ship. And so it happened that all were brought safely to land.
verses.28:1: And once we had been brought to safety, we then learned that the island is called Malta.
verses.28:2: And the native people showed us no ordinary kindness; for they kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because of the rain that had set in and because of the cold.
verses.28:3: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of brushwood and laid it on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened onto his hand.
verses.28:4: And when the native people saw the creature hanging from his hand, they began saying to one another, "Certainly this man is a murderer; although he was brought to safety from the sea, Justice has not permitted him to live."
verses.28:5: He, however, shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no harm.
verses.28:6: But they were expecting that he was about to swell up or suddenly fall down dead. Yet after waiting in expectation for a long time and seeing nothing unusual happening to him, they changed their minds and began saying that he was a god.
verses.28:7: Now in the region around that place were estates belonging to the leading man of the island, named Publius, who welcomed us and hosted us kindly for three days.
verses.28:8: And it happened that the father of Publius was lying in bed, afflicted with fevers and dysentery. Paul went in to him, and having prayed and laid his hands on him, he healed him.
verses.28:9: After this happened, the rest of those on the island who had illnesses also began coming and were being cured.
verses.28:10: They also honored us with many honors, and when we were setting sail, they put on board the things for our needs.
verses.28:11: After three months we set sail on an Alexandrian ship that had wintered at the island, with the Twin Brothers as its figurehead.
verses.28:12: And putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
verses.28:13: From there we weighed anchor and arrived at Rhegium. And after one day a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli.
verses.28:14: There we found brothers and were urged to stay with them seven days. And in this way we came to Rome.
verses.28:15: And from there the brothers, when they heard the news about us, came to meet us as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
verses.28:16: When we entered Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with the soldier who was guarding him.
verses.28:17: And it happened after three days that he called together the leading men of the Jews; and when they had assembled, he began saying to them, "Men, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people or the ancestral customs, I was handed over as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,
verses.28:18: who, when they had examined me, wanted to release me because there was no ground for death in me.
verses.28:19: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, not as having anything of which to accuse my nation.
verses.28:20: For this reason, therefore, I have asked to see you and to speak with you, for on account of the hope of Israel I am wearing this chain."
verses.28:21: And they said to him, "We have neither received letters concerning you from Judea, nor has any of the brothers arrived and reported or spoken anything evil about you.
verses.28:22: But we desire to hear from you what you think; for concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against."
verses.28:23: When they had set a day for him, they came to him at his lodging in greater numbers. He explained to them, solemnly testifying about the kingdom of God and seeking to persuade them concerning Jesus from both the Law of Moses and the Prophets, from morning until evening.
verses.28:24: And some were being persuaded by the things being spoken, while others would not believe.
verses.28:25: And disagreeing with one another, they began to depart after Paul had made one statement: "The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah the prophet to your fathers,
verses.28:26: saying, 'Go to this people and say, "Hearing, you will hear, yet never understand; and looking, you will look, yet never perceive;
verses.28:27: for the heart of this people has grown callous, and with their ears they have scarcely heard, and they have shut their eyes; otherwise they might see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart and turn back, and I would heal them."'
verses.28:28: Therefore let it be known to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles; they will also listen."
verses.28:30: And he remained a full two years in his own rented quarters, welcoming all who came in to him,
verses.28:31: proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with complete boldness, unhindered.

notes.1:2: The phrase "through the Holy Spirit" may modify either "having given commands" (as translated) or "whom He had chosen."
notes.1:4: The Greek participle synalizomenos is debated and may mean either "eating (salt) together with them" or "staying/assembling together with them."
notes.1:18: The Greek phrase prenes genomenos literally means "becoming prone" (i.e., "falling headlong/face down"), though some scholars interpret prenes as "swelling up" based on an alternative ancient usage.
notes.1:25: Some manuscripts read "allotted share" (kleron) instead of "place" (topon), echoing 1:17.
notes.2:24: Greek odinas literally means "birth pangs" (reflecting the Septuagint rendering of Hebrew chevel, which can mean either "cords/bonds" or "pangs"), paired with lysas ("having loosed"), evoking both the agony and the bondage of death.
notes.2:30: The critical Greek text preserves the shorter reading without "that according to the flesh He would raise up the Christ," leaving the infinitive kathisai ("to seat") directly dependent on God's oath to David.
notes.2:33: The dative te dexia may be taken either as locative ("to/at the right hand of God," echoing v. 34) or as instrumental ("by the right hand of God," referring to divine power).
notes.2:47: The critical Greek text concludes with epi to auto (literally "together" or "to the same place," used idiomatically for the assembled community as in vv. 1 and 44), whereas later manuscripts read "to the church."
notes.3:6: Many later manuscripts add "Rise up and" before "walk," whereas the earliest witnesses read simply "walk."
notes.3:13: Greek pais can mean "child" or "servant"; so also in 3:26, 4:27, and 4:30.
notes.3:15: Greek archegos denotes an originator, founder, or pioneering leader; "Founder of life" conveys the sense of the one who originates and leads into life.
notes.3:22: The critical Greek text reads "the Lord our God" (first-person plural), while some manuscripts harmonize with Deuteronomy 18:15 to read "your God."
notes.4:9: Greek sesostai (from sozo, "save" or "heal") means "has been made well" here and prepares for the wordplay with "salvation" and "be saved" in 4:12.
notes.4:25: The Greek syntax in the earliest manuscripts is highly compressed (literally "who of our father through the Holy Spirit of the mouth of David your servant said"); the translation smooths the clause while retaining all elements of the text.
notes.4:29: Greek doulois ("slaves") is distinct from pais ("Servant" or "servant") used for David in 4:25 and Jesus in 4:27 and 4:30.
notes.5:14: In Greek, "the Lord" (to kyrio) can modify either "believers" ("believers in the Lord") or "were being added" ("were being added to the Lord").
notes.5:28: The critical Greek text omits the negative particle found in later manuscripts, framing the clause as a direct accusation ("We strictly ordered you") rather than a rhetorical question.
notes.5:31: The Greek dative "te dexia autou" may be locative ("to His right hand") or instrumental ("by His right hand"); the title "archegon" carries the sense of "Leader," "Prince," or "Pioneer."
notes.5:36: Gamaliel places Theudas before Judas the Galilean (AD 6), which historians frequently discuss alongside Josephus's account of a later rebel named Theudas (c. AD 44-46).
notes.6:1: "Hellenists" refers to Greek-speaking Jews (often from the Diaspora), while "Hebrews" refers to Aramaic- or Hebrew-speaking Jews native to Judea and Galilee.
notes.6:8: The critical Greek text reads "grace" (charitos) rather than "faith" (pisteos), which appears in some later manuscripts by assimilation to 6:5.
notes.6:9: "Freedmen" (Libertinon) denotes former Jewish captives freed from Roman slavery or their descendants; the Greek syntax leaves open whether one synagogue or several distinct synagogues are listed.
notes.7:14: Stephen follows the Septuagint count of seventy-five persons (Gen 46:27 LXX; Exod 1:5 LXX), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text lists seventy.
notes.7:16: Stephen compresses two Old Testament accounts: Abraham's purchase of the burial cave at Machpelah from Ephron the Hittite (Gen 23) and Jacob's purchase of land at Shechem from the sons of Hamor, where Joseph's bones were buried (Gen 33:19; Josh 24:32).
notes.7:20: The Greek phrase asteios to theo (literally 'beautiful to God') is a Semitic idiom denoting either pleasing in God's sight or extraordinarily beautiful.
notes.7:30: The earliest witnesses read simply 'an angel,' while later manuscripts expand the phrase to 'an angel of the Lord' in harmonization with Exodus 3:2.
notes.7:38: Early manuscripts (including P74 and B) read 'to you' (hymin), whereas later witnesses assimilate to 'to us' (hemin).
notes.7:43: The Greek text reads 'Rompha' (with manuscript variants such as Rephan), reflecting the Septuagint of Amos 5:26; Stephen also replaces Amos 5:27's 'Damascus' with 'Babylon' in view of the Babylonian exile.
notes.7:45: The Greek name Iesous here renders the Hebrew name Joshua, Moses' successor.
notes.7:46: Early witnesses (including Sinaiticus*, B, and D) read 'for the house of Jacob' (oiko), while later manuscripts conform the wording to Psalm 132:5 by reading 'for the God of Jacob' (theo).
notes.8:7: The Greek exhibits a grammatical shift (anacoluthon), opening with "many of those who had unclean spirits" as nominative before switching to the neuter plural spirits crying out and coming out.
notes.8:26: The phrase kata mesembrian can mean either "toward the south" or "at noon." The closing clause ("This is a desert road," or "This is deserted") may be an editorial aside referring either to the road or to old Gaza.
notes.8:33: The quotation follows the Septuagint of Isaiah 53:8; the earliest manuscripts read "in humiliation" without a possessive pronoun.
notes.8:36: Verse 37, which adds Philip's condition and the eunuch's confession of faith, is absent from the earliest and most reliable Greek manuscripts and is not included in the Saints Greek Critical Text.
notes.9:5: Later manuscripts expand verses 5-6 with words drawn from Acts 26:14 and 22:10; the earliest Greek witnesses contain the shorter text translated here.
notes.9:7: Greek uses the genitive case with akouō ("hearing the voice/sound"), which is often contrasted with the accusative in Acts 22:9 to indicate that Saul's companions heard the sound without understanding the message.
notes.9:15: Literally "a vessel of choice" (skeuos eklogēs), an idiom denoting a chosen instrument or appointed agent.
notes.9:25: The earliest Greek manuscripts read "his disciples" (hoi mathētai autou), likely referring to converts won through Saul's preaching in Damascus; later manuscripts simplify this to "the disciples."
notes.9:31: The earliest manuscripts read the singular "the church" (hē ekklēsia) with singular verbs; later manuscripts read the plural "churches."
notes.10:19: The Greek text reads simply "men" without a numeral; other manuscripts read "three" or "two."
notes.10:20: The Greek phrase μηδὲν διακρινόμενος (middle voice) means "without hesitating at all"; compare the active μηδὲν διακρίναντα, "making no distinction," in 11:12.
notes.10:30: The idiomatic time expression "Four days ago to this very hour" indicates four days earlier at this same time of day (the ninth hour, about 3:00 p.m.); the critical text omits "fasting," which appears in later manuscripts.
notes.10:36: Verses 36–38 preserve an abrupt spoken Greek construction in which the opening accusative ("The word that He sent...") is interrupted by the parenthetical statement "He is Lord of all" and resumed in v. 37 by "you yourselves know the event that took place."
notes.11:12: The Greek active participle διακρίναντα literally means "making no distinction" (unlike the middle voice in 10:20, "without hesitating"), though some interpreters take it in the sense of "without doubting."
notes.11:20: The Greek text reads Ἑλληνιστάς ("Hellenists," i.e., Greek-speakers), while some manuscripts read Ἕλληνας ("Greeks"); here the term stands in contrast to "Jews" in v. 19.
notes.11:28: Greek οἰκουμένην ("inhabited world") in Luke-Acts typically refers to the Roman world.
notes.12:4: Greek τέσσαρσιν τετραδίοις ("four squads of four") denotes four four-man guard detachments (sixteen soldiers in total) rotating through the watches of the night.
notes.12:15: "His angel" reflects a contemporary Jewish belief that a person's guardian angel could appear in their likeness or speak with their voice.
notes.12:19: Greek ἀπαχθῆναι literally means "to be led away," a standard legal idiom in this period for being led away to execution.
notes.12:25: The Greek text reads εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ ("to/in Jerusalem") rather than the variant ἐξ Ἰερουσαλήμ ("from Jerusalem"); with the break after ὑπέστρεψαν, the phrase modifies πληρώσαντες τὴν διακονίαν ("having completed the service to Jerusalem") upon their return to Antioch.
notes.13:18: The Greek text reads ἐτροποφόρησεν ("put up with" or "endured their ways"); another well-attested variant reads ἐτροφοφόρησεν ("cared for" or "carried like a nurse," echoing Deut 1:31 LXX).
notes.13:20: In this textual order, "in about four hundred and fifty years" concludes the preceding summary of Israel's history through the conquest of Canaan, rather than measuring the period of the judges that follows.
notes.13:33: The Greek text reads τοῖς τέκνοις ἡμῶν ("for our children"); some manuscripts read τοῖς τέκνοις αὐτῶν ἡμῖν ("for us, their children").
notes.13:48: The perfect participle τεταγμένοι is taken here as passive ("had been appointed"); some interpreters understand it in a middle sense ("were disposed" or "aligned themselves").
notes.14:1: The Greek phrase kata to auto can mean "together" or "in the same manner" (as previously in Pisidian Antioch).
notes.14:9: The Greek verb sozo ("be made well") encompasses both physical healing and spiritual salvation in Luke-Acts.
notes.14:13: Literally "of Zeus who is before the city," referring to a temple or shrine of Zeus located just outside the city gates.
notes.14:23: The verb cheirotoneo originally referred to electing by raising hands and in Hellenistic Greek also came to mean simply "appoint."
notes.15:14: "Simeon" (Symeon) is the Semitic form of Peter's name Simon.
notes.15:16: James quotes Amos 9:11-12 following the Septuagint, which reads "the rest of mankind" rather than the Masoretic Text's "the remnant of Edom."
notes.15:20: "Pollutions" (alisgema) is a rare word occurring only here in the New Testament, clarified in the council's letter (v. 29) as "things sacrificed to idols."
notes.15:23: The critical text reads "the apostles and the elders, brothers" in apposition, whereas later manuscripts insert "and the" before "brothers."
notes.15:33: The earliest manuscripts lack verse 34 ("But it seemed good to Silas to remain there"); the Saints Greek Critical Text prints it within double brackets ⟦ ⟧ (shown as an additional verse).
notes.16:7: The earliest and best manuscripts read 'the Spirit of Jesus,' whereas some later witnesses omit 'of Jesus' to read simply 'the Spirit.'
notes.16:10: The shift from third person ('they') to first person plural ('we') marks the first of the 'we' sections in Acts.
notes.16:12: The Greek phrase translated 'a leading city of the district of Macedonia' is grammatically and textually debated; the attested text supports 'leading city' (or 'first city'), while some interpreters emend it to 'a city of the first district of Macedonia.'
notes.16:16: Literally 'a spirit, a Python,' referring to a spirit of prophecy or divination associated in the Greco-Roman world with Apollo's oracle at Delphi.
notes.16:35: Greek rhabdouchoi, literally 'rod-bearers,' referring to Roman lictors who served as official attendants to the chief magistrates and carried out public beatings.
notes.17:6: "City officials" translates Greek politarchas (politarchs), the title of the city's magistrates.
notes.17:18: "Babbler" translates spermologos (literally "seed-picker"), Athenian slang for a scavenger of stray ideas. "Foreign deities" (xenon daimonion) reflects classical Greek usage for divine beings rather than evil spirits.
notes.17:22: Greek deisidaimonesterous is an ambiguous comparative ranging from "very religious" to "rather superstitious."
notes.17:26: Greek ex henos, "from one," is usually understood as one man; some later manuscripts add "blood" (haimatos).
notes.18:5: "With the word" follows the earliest manuscripts (to logo); later Byzantine manuscripts read "in the spirit" (to pneumati).
notes.18:17: The earliest manuscripts read simply "they all" (pantes), leaving unspecified whether the assailants were local Greeks or Jews; later manuscripts add "the Greeks."
notes.18:18: The singular participle "having cut his hair" (keiramenos) syntactically refers to Paul as the subject of the sentence, though some interpreters connect it with the immediately preceding name, Aquila.
notes.18:22: "Went up" (anabas) is customary idiom for ascending to Jerusalem before going down (katebe) to Antioch, though Jerusalem is not explicitly named in the verse.
notes.19:16: The Greek word translated "all of them" (amphoteros) literally means "both of them," though in Koine Greek it can mean "all" of more than two, or indicate that only two of Sceva's seven sons were present here.
notes.19:21: The Greek phrase "en to pneumati" may refer either to Paul's own spirit ("resolved in his spirit") or to the Holy Spirit ("resolved in the Spirit").
notes.19:33: The critical text reads "synebibasan" ("prompted" or "instructed"), which is unusual here; some later manuscripts read "proebibasan" ("pushed forward").
notes.19:35: The Greek "diopetes" ("that which fell from heaven") literally means "fallen from Zeus" or "from the sky," referring to the sacred image or stone associated with Artemis.
notes.19:40: The critical Greek text retains a negative ("peri hou ou dynesometha"), producing a compressed syntax meaning there is no justification and regarding it they will be unable to give an account for the uproar.
notes.20:5: The critical Greek text reads proselthontes (lit. 'having come forward/arrived'), while other manuscripts read proelthontes ('having gone ahead').
notes.20:22: Or 'bound by the Spirit'; the Greek dative to pneumati can refer either to Paul's own spirit (cf. 19:21) or to the Holy Spirit.
notes.20:24: The Greek phrasing blends two idioms ('consider my life of no account' and 'consider my life precious to myself').
notes.20:28: Some manuscripts read 'the church of the Lord' instead of 'the church of God.' The closing phrase dia tou haimatos tou idiou may be rendered either 'through His own blood' or 'through the blood of His Own [i.e., His Son].'
notes.20:35: This saying of Jesus is not recorded in any of the four Gospels.
notes.21:16: The Greek clause exhibits inverse attraction and can be read either as "bringing us to a certain Mnason, with whom we were to lodge" (the standard view) or "bringing along a certain Mnason... with whom we were to lodge."
notes.21:22: Later manuscripts add "the multitude must certainly assemble," which is absent from the earliest Greek witnesses and the Saints Greek Critical Text.
notes.21:31: Greek chiliarchos ("commander") refers to a Roman military tribune in charge of a cohort (speira, nominally up to 1,000 soldiers).
notes.21:38: Greek sikarioi (from Latin sicarii, literally "dagger-men") designated a militant Jewish faction known for political assassinations.
notes.21:40: "The Hebrew dialect" in first-century Greek usage commonly refers to Aramaic, the Semitic vernacular of Judea, though Hebrew itself is also possible.
notes.22:9: Here akouo ("hear") takes the accusative ("the voice"), whereas Acts 9:7 uses the genitive; many interpreters understand the construction here as "did not understand the voice" in contrast to hearing the sound.
notes.22:13: The Greek verb anablepo creates a wordplay here, meaning both "receive your sight" in Ananias's command and "looked up" in Paul's action.
notes.22:25: The dative tois himasin can be understood either instrumentally as "with the leather straps" (binding him to the post) or as "for the leather thongs/whips."
